author: ACD
premise: A young bank clerk notices that the same elderly customer deposits a single gold sovereign every morning and withdraws it every evening. When the customer fails to appear one day, the clerk seeks out a private inquiry agent, convinced the ritual concealed something far more serious than eccentricity.

author: ACD
premise: A respected surgeon is found unconscious in his locked consulting room, his instrument case open and one scalpel missing. His partner insists nothing else was taken, but a junior assistant quietly reports that a patient's records have been altered. An investigator must decide whom to believe.

author: ACD
premise: A florist who supplies flowers to a large hotel notices that one guest orders a fresh white lily every morning for a room the hotel records as empty. When the florist's errand boy is turned away by a porter he has never seen before, she consults a private investigator.
setting: Covent Garden and the Strand, London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A theatrical manager receives an anonymous warning that his leading actress will not survive the opening night. She dismisses it as a rival's spite, but the stage doorman has seen a stranger studying the trapdoor machinery. An inquiry agent attends the dress rehearsal in disguise.

author: ACD
premise: A retired sea captain hires an investigator to find his estranged son, last seen working at the docks. The search uncovers a warehouse whose owner pays its men in cash, employs no clerk, and ships crates that are always lighter on arrival than on departure.

author: ACD
premise: A widow brings a detective a handful of pressed flowers that arrive by post every week, each from a different county. Her late husband collected botanical specimens, and the senders' locations, plotted on a map, trace a route he took the year before his death.

author: ACD
premise: A wealthy collector reports that a celebrated painting in his gallery has been replaced by a near-perfect copy, yet the gallery has been guarded day and night. The only visitors in a month were a picture restorer, a chimney sweep, and the collector's own nephew.

author: ACD
premise: A lodging-house keeper grows uneasy about a quiet lodger who pays three months in advance, never receives letters, and burns a candle in his window every night until two. When he vanishes leaving his trunk behind, she sends for an investigator before the police.
setting: A lodging house in Bloomsbury, London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A junior civil servant is accused of selling the contents of a confidential naval report, though he swears the document never left his sight. His fiancée engages an investigator, who becomes interested in the office's new copying clerk and the clerk's habit of whistling.

author: ACD
premise: A fashionable dressmaker finds that customers' measurements have been stolen from her books, and soon afterwards several clients are robbed at private balls. The thief seems to know exactly which gowns conceal jewelled ornaments. She consults a detective rather than lose her reputation.

author: ACD
premise: A clergyman's daughter reports that her father returned from a parish visit pale and silent, and has since refused to preach. Every night he sits writing a letter that he burns at dawn. She begs an investigator to learn what happened in a poor street by the river.

author: ACD
premise: A chess club secretary finds that a member has won every game for a month by moves no one could have predicted. When a defeated opponent collapses at the board after drinking his tea, the club's committee asks an investigator to attend the next tournament quietly.
setting: A gentlemen's club near the Strand, London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A railway signalman swears he saw a lamp signalling from an empty carriage on a goods train at midnight. His superiors think him drunk, but a parcel of bonds has disappeared from the same train. An investigator rides the line on the following night.

author: ACD
premise: A pawnbroker brings an investigator a silver watch pledged by a ragged boy, engraved with the crest of a family whose heir drowned abroad two years earlier. The boy insists a gentleman gave it to him for carrying a message, but he cannot read the address.

author: ACD
premise: An inventor claims that a rival has stolen the design of his electrical lamp, though the drawings remain locked in his safe. The rival, meanwhile, has disappeared, and his workshop shows signs of a hurried departure. An investigator must decide which man is the injured party.

author: ACD
premise: A newspaper editor notices that personal advertisements placed in his columns have begun using numbers instead of words. A reader's letter suggests they are messages between thieves. When the editor's typesetter is found beaten in an alley, the editor seeks out a private detective.

author: ACD
premise: A young wife discovers that her husband, a respectable wine merchant, has two sets of account books and a second house key she cannot match to any door. Fearing scandal more than the truth, she hires an investigator to find out where the key belongs.

author: ACD
premise: A foreign diplomat's valet is found dead in a cab, apparently of heart failure. The diplomat claims to know nothing, yet within a day the embassy has burned a quantity of papers. An investigator is engaged by the valet's sister, who suspects her brother knew too much.

author: ACD
premise: A music teacher reports that her pupil, a wealthy girl of seventeen, plays a different tune at every lesson, which the girl says a stranger hums beneath her window. The girl's guardian forbids further lessons. The teacher, worried, takes the tunes to an investigator.

author: ACD
premise: A hotel porter brings a detective a guest's luggage left unclaimed after the guest checked out in apparent haste. Inside are a lady's gloves, a revolver with one chamber fired, and a railway timetable with a single train underlined. The guest registered under a false address.

author: ACD
premise: A bookseller finds that rare volumes returned by a regular customer have had single pages removed with a razor. The missing pages share nothing obvious, but each contains a map. When the customer stops visiting, the bookseller asks an investigator to discover what he is assembling.

author: ACD
premise: An elderly lady is convinced that someone enters her house each night and moves her furniture by an inch. Her family think her failing, but an investigator notices that the house stands beside a bank whose vaults have recently been enlarged.
setting: A terrace house near Lombard Street, London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A cab driver comes to an investigator in distress: a passenger he set down at a certain address was reported dead at another address across London the same hour. The police suspect the cabman of lying. The investigator begins by examining the cab itself.

author: ACD
premise: A schoolmaster suspects one of his senior boys of forging cheques, but the boy's handwriting is plainly unlike the forgeries. When the headmaster's study is burgled, the schoolmaster asks a private investigator to examine both the evidence and the school's jealous rivalries.
setting: A boys' school on the edge of London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A lady's maid is dismissed after her mistress's necklace disappears, though she swears she never touched it. Her brother, a police constable, privately doubts the official case and seeks help from an investigator, who notices that the necklace's insurance was increased only a week before.

author: ACD
premise: A brewer's heir receives a series of telegrams, each announcing a death that has not yet occurred. The first two names belong to men who die within days. The third name is his own, and he comes to an investigator in a state of barely controlled fear.
setting: London and a brewery town in Kent, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: An estate steward discovers that the lake on his employer's property is being drained at night by someone who refills it before morning. His employer refuses to involve the police. The steward calls in an investigator, who learns that an old chapel once stood where the water now lies.

author: ACD
premise: A young heiress arrives to take possession of a remote manor she has inherited, only to find the household staff convinced she is an impostor. A portrait in the hall resembles her closely, but the family solicitor has died suddenly. She writes to an investigator for help.
setting: A manor house on the Northumberland coast, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A racehorse trainer reports that his best colt runs brilliantly in private trials but falters in every public race. The stable lads are loyal, the feed is tested, and the jockey is honest. An investigator spends a week at the stables observing who visits after dark.

author: ACD
premise: A village postmistress notices that letters addressed to the squire are always slightly damp, as though steamed open and resealed. When the squire's gamekeeper vanishes, she sends a cautious letter of her own to an investigator in London, hoping it will not be intercepted.

author: ACD
premise: A mining engineer is called to inspect a disused tin mine whose owner wishes to reopen it. He finds fresh candle wax in a gallery sealed for twenty years, and a ladder newer than any in the county. He suspects the mine is already being worked by someone.

author: ACD
premise: A cathedral organist claims the organ plays a few notes by itself at night. The choir thinks it a ghost story, but a valuable altar plate has meanwhile been replaced with a gilt copy. An investigator is asked by the dean to look into both matters discreetly.
setting: A cathedral city in the west of England, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A wealthy merchant returned from the goldfields receives a parcel containing a nugget and a scrap of canvas bearing four initials. He refuses to explain them to his family, but begins carrying a revolver. His daughter hires an investigator when he fails to return from a walk.
setting: Bayswater, London, with a past in the Australian goldfields, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A retired tea planter hears that a former partner, whom he believed dead, has been seen in Liverpool. Within a week his house is watched by a lascar sailor. He asks an investigator to find out what the partner wants, while refusing to describe how their partnership ended.
setting: Liverpool and a past in Ceylon, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A man is found dead in an empty house with an American newspaper folded beside him, a single date ringed in ink. Scotland Yard is puzzled, but a private investigator recognises the newspaper's town as the site of a notorious bank robbery twenty years before.
setting: An empty house in Lambeth, London, 1880s

author: ACD
premise: A former army surgeon who served in Afghanistan is approached by a stranger who claims to have been his patient, and asks for help recovering something buried near a fort. The surgeon remembers no such patient and consults an investigator about the stranger's intentions.
setting: London, with a past on the North-West Frontier, 1880s

author: ACD
premise: A ship's officer returning from South America delivers a sealed letter to an English family on behalf of a dying passenger. The family burns it unread, and that night someone ransacks the officer's lodgings. He asks an investigator what he has unwittingly carried home.

author: ACD
premise: An elderly baronet is visited by a man claiming to be the son of a brother lost on a voyage to the Cape. The claimant knows family secrets, but the baronet's housekeeper insists the brother had no child. An investigator must test the claim before the will is changed.
setting: A country house in Sussex, with a past at the Cape, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A former soldier, now a respectable shopkeeper, recognises a customer as a man he once saw commit a murder in India. The customer appears not to recognise him, but the shop is burgled the next night and an old regimental photograph taken. He goes to an investigator.
setting: Croydon, with a past in India, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A young Englishwoman returns from her father's sheep station to claim a London inheritance, and is met at the dock by a solicitor she does not know. Within days she suspects the man is not a solicitor at all, and writes in secret to a detective.
setting: London, with a past in New Zealand, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A sailor dies in a seamen's hospital clutching a carved ivory token, raving about a debt owed by a man in England. The hospital chaplain traces the name to a prosperous alderman, who denies all knowledge. An investigator suspects the alderman is lying, and frightened.

author: ACD
premise: A gentleman returned from mining in Mexico is found in his study unable to speak, having apparently suffered a stroke. On his desk is a letter in Spanish and a sketch of a church. His wife engages an investigator to discover what news so overwhelmed him.
setting: A house in Richmond, with a past in Mexico, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: An art student lodging above a jeweller's shop hears hammering through the floor every night, though the shop is closed. The jeweller tells her he repairs clocks after hours. When the hammering stops and the jeweller disappears, she reports to an investigator.

author: ACD
premise: A wealthy philanthropist asks an investigator to find a man who saved his life in a street accident and vanished without giving his name. The search reveals the rescuer has been seen in several places at once, and the philanthropist's gratitude begins to look like fear.

author: ACD
premise: A conjuror performing at a music hall is accused of stealing a duchess's bracelet during a trick in which he borrowed it from the audience. He swears the bracelet he returned was the same one. An investigator examines the trick and the conjuror's assistant.
setting: A music hall in the East End, London, 1890s

author: ACD
premise: A family of gypsies is blamed when a village church's silver chalice disappears. The vicar doubts their guilt and writes to an investigator, mentioning that the churchwarden has recently paid off a large debt and that the bell-ringers swear they heard a horse at midnight.

author: ACD
premise: An engineer building a new railway viaduct finds his surveying stakes moved each night, always to divert the line away from a particular farm. The farmer protests innocence, and the railway company threatens to dismiss the engineer, who engages an investigator.

author: ACD
premise: A society hostess receives an invitation in her own handwriting to a dinner she never planned. Several guests arrive at her door that evening, among them a man who was supposed to be in prison. She sends for an investigator before the soup is served.

author: ACD
premise: An undertaker reports that a coffin he delivered for burial weighed far more than its occupant could have. The family hurried the funeral and refused his offer of a viewing. Troubled, he approaches a private investigator before the grave is filled.

author: ACD
premise: A missionary home on leave from China is followed through London by a man who never quite approaches him. The missionary's luggage, delivered from the ship, has been searched and repacked with great care. An investigator is consulted by the missionary's anxious wife.
setting: London, with a past in China, 1890s

author: CB
premise: A young woman employed as a nursery governess discovers that her employer's eldest son, whom she has privately admired, is engaged to a rich neighbour. She must continue teaching his younger sisters under the same roof while concealing what she feels from everyone, including herself.

author: CB
premise: An English teacher at a girls' boarding school abroad is accused by a pupil of reading her private letters. The headmistress believes the pupil. The teacher, friendless in a foreign city and unable to argue fluently in its language, must defend her honour or lose her post.
setting: A boarding school in a Flemish city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: The unmarried daughter of a mill owner watches her father reduce wages as orders fail. She is moved by the hunger of the workers and offended by the indifference of her suitors, yet she has no money or power of her own with which to act.

author: CB
premise: A young English bookkeeper working for a merchant house abroad is asked by his employer to tutor the merchant's sons in English. The boys are idle, the mother interferes, and the bookkeeper must decide whether to tell the merchant the truth about his sons' progress.

author: CB
premise: A curate newly arrived in a manufacturing parish finds himself despised by the workers as the master's man and ignored by the masters as a poor parson. A widow who keeps the parish school becomes his only honest critic, and gradually his conscience.

author: CB
premise: A young woman nursing her dying aunt through a long winter learns that her inheritance will go instead to a cousin who never visited. She is free and penniless at once, and must decide whether to accept a place offered by a family she knows to be cold.
setting: An isolated farmhouse on the Yorkshire moors, 1830s

author: CB
premise: A teacher abroad receives news that her small savings, left in an English bank, have been lost in its failure. She tells no one, continues teaching, and calculates how many months she can survive before she must ask the director for an advance she is too proud to request.
setting: A girls' school in a Continental city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: Two young women, one an heiress and one a poor rector's niece, form an unlikely friendship. When both come to care for the same struggling manufacturer, their friendship is tested by pride, money, and the knowledge that only the heiress could save his business.
setting: A manufacturing district in the West Riding, 1810s

author: CB
premise: A schoolteacher's sister, a quiet invalid, writes poems she shows no one. When a visiting critic praises them by chance, the elder sister, who has given up her own ambitions to care for the family, is torn between pride and an ugly jealousy she is ashamed to feel.

author: CB
premise: A governess overhears her employers discussing her as though she were furniture. That night their youngest child falls dangerously ill, and only the governess knows how to nurse him. She must decide whether to stay out of duty or leave out of self-respect.

author: CB
premise: An English teacher at a foreign school is asked to supervise the director's own daughter, a clever, deceitful girl of fifteen. The girl tests every rule and reports every lapse to her mother. The teacher must manage her without either cruelty or surrender.
setting: A girls' school in a Flemish city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A mill owner's ward, rich and impulsive, decides to manage her own estate and tenants. The local gentry are scandalised, the parson amused, and her own uncle obstructs her at every turn. She learns that independence in a woman is regarded as a kind of madness.
setting: A manor in a Yorkshire manufacturing valley, 1810s

author: CB
premise: A young woman who has spent her girlhood in a charitable institution is placed as a seamstress's apprentice. Her mistress is kind but poor, and the girl must choose between staying in that narrow life or accepting the patronage of a lady whose motives are unclear.

author: CB
premise: A governess at a country house is visited at night by her employer's sister, who confesses that the household's apparent harmony conceals a bitter marriage. The governess is asked to carry letters in secret. She must decide where her loyalty and her conscience lie.
setting: A country house in the East Riding of Yorkshire, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An English girl sent abroad to finish her education is courted by a charming and penniless count. Her teacher, an older Englishwoman, sees through him and warns her. The girl refuses to listen, and the teacher must decide whether to write to the girl's father.
setting: A pensionnat in a French-speaking city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: During a hard winter of unemployment, a group of starving weavers petitions a manufacturer for work. He refuses, citing the war and the blockade. His sister, who keeps his house, quietly begins distributing food, knowing he would forbid it if he knew.

author: CB
premise: A widowed mother and her grown daughter take in lodgers to survive after a bank failure. One lodger, a reserved schoolmaster, begins helping the daughter with her studies. The mother suspects a romance; the daughter wants only to qualify as a teacher and escape the house.

author: CB
premise: A governess is falsely accused of encouraging the attentions of her employer's son. The son is too cowardly to clear her name. Dismissed without a reference, she sets out on foot towards the nearest town, with a few shillings and her pride intact.

author: CB
premise: A young English widow takes a post as housekeeper to a foreign doctor who runs a clinic for the poor. His sister distrusts the Englishwoman as a Protestant and a stranger. The widow must win the household's trust while keeping secret why she left England.
setting: A quarter of an old Flemish town, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A manufacturer who has lost everything in a failed speculation proposes to a wealthy woman he does not love. She accepts, then discovers his motive. The story turns on whether she will release him in scorn or hold him to his word.
setting: A mill town in the West Riding, 1810s

author: CB
premise: An unmarried woman of thirty, keeping house for her widowed brother, a curate, learns that he intends to marry. His bride will become mistress of the household. The sister must find a new life for herself with neither money, training, nor encouragement.

author: CB
premise: A governess discovers that her pupil, a sullen boy of nine, is terrified of his father. She tries to win the boy's confidence, and in doing so learns that his mother did not die of illness, as the household claims, but left the house one night and never returned.
setting: A house in the North York Moors, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An English teacher at a foreign school receives a letter from home informing her that her only brother has died. No one at the school knows her well enough to comfort her. She must continue teaching the next morning, and the effort of composure becomes the story.
setting: A girls' school in a Continental city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A young doctor in a manufacturing town treats the injuries of children who work in the mills. He presses the owners to shorten their hours and is told to mind his trade. A mill owner's daughter secretly gives him money for a dispensary.

author: CB
premise: A governess falls ill with fever and is nursed by the family's housekeeper, a hard woman who has never been kind to her. In her recovery the governess learns the housekeeper was once a governess herself, and how the household broke her.
setting: An old manor house in Cumberland, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An Englishwoman teaching abroad is courted, half in jest, by a wealthy English traveller passing through the city. He offers to take her home to England as his wife. She suspects he is bored, and fears that she is only lonely.
setting: A Continental city and its English hotel, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A rector who preaches obedience to the poor is challenged in the vestry by a self-taught weaver who quotes scripture back at him. The rector's daughter, who overhears, begins secretly reading the books the weaver recommends.
setting: A moorland parish above a mill valley, 1810s

author: CB
premise: A young woman who has trained herself as a teacher opens a small day school with her savings. Within months a rival school opens across the street, backed by the rector. She must decide whether to compete, beg, or close.

author: CB
premise: A governess at a wealthy household is befriended by a visiting cousin of the family, an artist. He paints her portrait and tells her she has a remarkable face. She does not trust flattery, and suspects the portrait is meant to provoke someone else in the house.

author: CB
premise: An English pupil at a foreign school is caught by her teacher hiding a letter from a young man. The teacher is supposed to report her. Remembering her own loneliness at that age, she must decide whether to protect the girl and risk her own position.
setting: A pensionnat in a Flemish city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A clergyman's widow inherits a share in a failing mill and refuses to sell it to the partner who has cheated her husband. She learns bookkeeping, attends the cloth market, and endures the contempt of every merchant in the hall.
setting: A cloth-market town in the West Riding, 1820s

author: CB
premise: A young woman's father arranges her marriage to a prosperous merchant twenty years her senior, who is generous and dull. She feels no affection for him, but her family's debts are pressing. On the eve of the wedding she must decide whether gratitude is enough to build a life upon.

author: CB
premise: A governess accompanies her employer's family to the seaside, where she meets a former schoolfellow who has married well. The friend pities her openly. The governess must endure the pity, and examine whether any part of it is deserved.

author: CB
premise: A young English master at a foreign school is offered promotion if he will marry the director's niece. He respects her but loves a poor teacher who has no connections. His prospects, and his principles, depend on his answer.
setting: A school in a Belgian city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A militia officer is billeted in a manufacturing village to keep order during unrest. He is ordered to arrest a weaver accused of sedition, and finds that the weaver's daughter teaches the Sunday school his own sister attends.

author: CB
premise: A governess's employer, a widower, asks her to accompany him on a journey to place his daughter in a school. On the road he speaks to her as an equal for the first time. On the return journey he becomes cold again, and she cannot understand why.
setting: Coach roads between Yorkshire and London, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An English teacher abroad is drawn into a quarrel between two colleagues, each of whom wants her support for a promotion. She dislikes both and is honest with neither. When one of them is dismissed, she must live with the consequences of her silence.
setting: A girls' school in a Continental city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A Sunday-school teacher learns that a boy in her class has been beaten by an overlooker at the mill. She goes to the mill herself to complain, and is received by the owner's son, who listens politely and does nothing.
setting: A mill town in the West Riding, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A young widow with a small child refuses an offer from her late husband's family to raise the boy, which would require her to give him up. She takes in sewing and lives on very little. The family's lawyer begins calling on her.

author: CB
premise: A governess notices that the family's elder daughter, a beautiful girl of eighteen, is being pressed to marry a much older man for his fortune. The girl confides in the governess, who has no power to help and no right to interfere.

author: CB
premise: An English teacher abroad is visited by an Englishwoman who claims to be a distant cousin and seems to know a great deal about the teacher's family. The cousin is charming and asks for a loan. The teacher, starved of home, wants to believe her.

author: CB
premise: A manufacturer's wife, ignored by her husband and despised by his workers, begins visiting the sick in the cottages near the mill. Her charity is received with suspicion. One woman refuses her help outright, and it becomes her purpose to understand why.

author: CB
premise: At a school examination before parents and dignitaries, an English teacher's pupil recites a poem the teacher wrote herself. The director takes credit for it. The teacher must decide whether to claim her work or keep her place.
setting: A school in a Belgian city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: A young woman of independent means buys a ruined mill to give work to the unemployed of her parish. The neighbouring gentry predict disaster and her suitor withdraws. In her first winter the machinery fails and the workers begin to doubt her.
setting: A valley in the West Riding, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An English teacher abroad attends a lecture by a famous orator, and at the door meets a fellow countryman she once rejected as a suitor. He is now prosperous and married. They speak for ten minutes in the cold, and she walks home alone.

author: CB
premise: A shy young curate falls in love with the daughter of the mill owner whose policies he has denounced from the pulpit. The daughter, who agrees with his sermons, refuses to marry against her father's wishes.

author: CB
premise: A young woman emigrating to New Zealand as a teacher spends her last week in England with her old schoolmistress, who disapproves. On the eve of sailing they finally speak openly about what each has sacrificed for her own independence.
setting: A Yorkshire town and the port of Liverpool, 1850s

author: CB
premise: A governess is asked by her pupil's mother to keep a diary of the child's progress, and finds that the mother reads it in secret for hints of her husband's movements. The governess begins to write the diary for two readers.

author: CB
premise: A young Englishwoman who has become the most respected teacher at a foreign school is offered a post in England at higher pay. Her pupils beg her to stay, and so, wordlessly, does a colleague she has never quite befriended.
setting: A girls' school in a Flemish city, 1840s

author: CB
premise: An heiress who has refused every suitor is visited by a former tutor, now a poor schoolmaster, who once taught her brother. She finds that he is the only man who speaks to her without flattery, and that her fortune stands between them.
setting: A manor in the West Riding, 1810s

author: CD
premise: A boy of ten is sent to live with a grandfather he has never met, a retired pawnbroker who lives above his shuttered shop and trusts nobody. The boy must earn the old man's affection while discovering why every pledge in the shop has been kept for thirty years.
setting: A narrow street near Holborn, London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A young clerk in a shipping office wins a modest prize in a public lottery and resolves to keep it secret from his grasping relations. Within a week every one of them has heard of it, and each arrives at his lodging with a misfortune requiring exactly the amount he has won.

author: CD
premise: A pompous alderman who has organised a banquet to celebrate a new town hall discovers on the morning of the feast that the contractor has run off with the funds and the roof is unfinished. He must preside over the banquet in the rain without admitting anything is wrong.

author: CD
premise: An English banker's clerk is sent to France to recover deposits belonging to a noble family who have fled the country. He finds the family's steward running their chateau as his own, and the villagers hungry and watchful. The clerk must decide whose property he is really protecting.

author: CD
premise: An orphan girl employed as a drudge in a boarding house is adopted on a whim by a wealthy, eccentric spinster who soon tires of her. Returned to the boarding house with fine manners and no prospects, the girl must decide which world she now belongs to.
setting: A boarding house in Camden Town, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A widowed washerwoman with five children takes in a half-starved boy found sleeping in her copper. Her neighbours call her a fool, and the parish beadle wants the boy returned to the workhouse. She hides him and swears he is her nephew.
setting: A court off Seven Dials, London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A young man apprenticed to a coffin-maker longs to become an actor. When a travelling company passes through, its manager offers him a small part. His master forbids it, his mother weeps, and the girl he admires says he would be ridiculous.

author: CD
premise: A night-school teacher in a manufacturing town is told by the mill owners who fund the school that he must teach only arithmetic and the catechism. His best pupil, a grown man who works the boilers, asks to be taught to read poetry.
setting: A manufacturing town in the north, 1850s

author: CD
premise: A shy boy of twelve is sent to sea as a cabin boy on a coastal collier after his father's death. The cook, a one-eyed giant with a terrible temper, turns out to be the only person aboard who ever asks how he is.
setting: A collier brig between Newcastle and London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A retired sea cook opens a pie shop beside the river with his life savings. A clever, ragged boy offers to sell pies from a tray on commission. Business doubles, until the cook discovers the boy is also running errands for a fence on the other side of the bridge.

author: CD
premise: A young woman who has been engaged for seven years to a man always waiting for his prospects to improve finally gives him an ultimatum. He promises to marry her when his uncle dies. The uncle, overhearing, decides to live forever out of spite.
setting: A suburban villa in Islington, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A French émigré working as a dancing master in London is visited by a man claiming to come from his native village, bearing news that his imprisoned brother may be freed for a price. The dancing master's English landlady suspects a swindle, and says so.

author: CD
premise: A copying clerk who has worked thirty years for the same firm is told he will be replaced by a younger man. He has never missed a day, and his only pleasure is a canary. He goes home to tell his sister, and cannot bring himself to say it.
setting: Lincoln's Inn Fields and Pentonville, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A cooper in a brewery town discovers his master has been watering the ale sold to the workhouse. He is the only man who knows. Speaking up will cost his place and his children's bread, and staying silent will cost him something he cannot name.

author: CD
premise: A gang of boys who sleep under the arches of a railway viaduct adopt a lost little girl who cannot remember her own name. They feed her by begging and petty theft. When a well-dressed lady begins asking questions about the child in the neighbourhood, the boys must decide whether to give her up.

author: CD
premise: A young man who believes himself destined to be a great poet takes a cheap lodging and waits for inspiration. His landlady, his creditors, and a sensible girl who sells gloves across the street all have opinions about his talent. None of them agrees with his.
setting: A lodging house in the Borough, London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A parish clerk who prides himself on economy is put in charge of distributing coal to the poor in a hard winter. His own elderly mother, whom he has not visited in years, turns out to be on the list.

author: CD
premise: A widow's only son, idolised and spoilt, goes to London to become a gentleman. He spends his mother's savings in a year. Ashamed to return, he takes work as a waiter in the very hotel where he once dined at the best table and tipped the porters lavishly.
setting: A Suffolk village and a London hotel, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A French hairdresser in London who has prospered by flattering the aristocracy learns that his own brother is a leader of the revolutionary club in their home town. His customers begin to look at him strangely, and his brother writes asking for money.

author: CD
premise: A dealer in old rags and bones, a miser by reputation, dies in his yard and is discovered to have hidden money in every heap. His neighbours descend on the yard. A young servant girl who once nursed him knows where the largest sum is hidden.
setting: A rag-and-bone yard in Clerkenwell, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A boy sent to work in a soap boilery after his father's bankruptcy pretends to his workmates that he is the son of a sea captain lost at sea. He tells the story so well that he begins to believe it, until an old sailor who drinks at the corner pub asks for the captain's name.
setting: A riverside works near Battersea, London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A pawnbroker's widow who has always lent money at ruinous interest finds herself, after a fall, dependent on the charity of a neighbour she once refused a loan. The neighbour nurses her without reproach, which the widow finds harder to bear than cruelty.
setting: A street in Somers Town, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A young lawyer defends a coal-heaver accused of stealing from his employer. The case is hopeless until the lawyer's office boy, sent to deliver a summons, notices that the employer's own clerk is wearing a new pair of boots.
setting: The Old Bailey and Wapping, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: Two brothers inherit a small grocery shop. The elder runs it with care while the younger dreams and borrows. When the younger is engaged to a rich man's daughter, he asks the elder to sell the shop to pay for the wedding.

author: CD
premise: A blind fiddler and his granddaughter earn their living playing outside public houses. When the fiddler falls ill, the girl must play alone. A smooth-talking showman offers her a place in his travelling exhibition.

author: CD
premise: An English bookseller travelling to France to collect a debt from a Paris printer finds the city in uproar and the printer arrested. The printer's young apprentice begs the bookseller to carry a parcel of papers back to England. The bookseller has never done a brave thing in his life.

author: CD
premise: A young man raised by a stern aunt who keeps a lodging house discovers that his father, believed dead, is alive and working as a ticket collector at a provincial railway station. He goes to see him without announcing himself.
setting: London and a railway town in the Midlands, 1850s

author: CD
premise: A mill hand's wife, worn out by work and grief, is offered a place as housekeeper to the mill owner's widowed brother. Her husband forbids it out of pride. Their children are hungry, and the brother is kind.

author: CD
premise: An orphan boy apprenticed to a chimney sweep runs away and is taken in by a family of barge people. He grows strong on the canal and learns to read from the barge-master's daughter. Years later, the sweep's assistant recognises him at a lock.

author: CD
premise: An old Parisian clockmaker who keeps the clocks of the city hall running through every change of government is asked by a revolutionary official to set them to a new calendar. He refuses, and must explain to his apprentice why a clock is worth risking one's neck for.

author: CD
premise: A hard-hearted moneylender's clerk is ordered to evict a family behind on their rent. On the staircase he meets the family's eldest girl, who offers him the only coin she has. He returns to the office with the money and without the eviction.
setting: A tenement in Saffron Hill, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A young widow who runs her late husband's ironmongery in a manufacturing town is courted by the town's leading cotton master, a man who speaks of marriage as a merger. She is tempted by security and repelled by his arithmetic of feeling.

author: CD
premise: A young doctor returns from India to find his childhood sweetheart engaged to his former employer. He takes a poor practice nearby, and treats the girl's younger brother through a long illness. The family's gratitude complicates everything.

author: CD
premise: A conscientious magistrate is shocked to find that the boy brought before him for stealing a loaf is the son of his own former coachman. He must deal with the boy according to the law or find a way around it that will not disgrace him.
setting: A police court in Clerkenwell, London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A Christmas goose club, run by a publican, collapses when the publican disappears with the subscriptions. The members, all poor, gather in the empty tavern to decide what to do, and an elderly lamplighter proposes a remedy of his own.
setting: A tavern in Camden Town, London, at Christmas, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A young woman brought up in comfort by a rich uncle learns that he has lost everything in a railway speculation. She must find work. A former governess, now running a school, offers her a place as an assistant teacher at a tiny salary.

author: CD
premise: An English coachman who once drove a French nobleman's carriage is asked, years later in London, to give evidence about an accident in which a child was killed. His memory and his loyalties are both uncertain.

author: CD
premise: A young man trained as a gentleman by a rich patron learns that the patron's fortune came from slave plantations. He must decide whether to keep the money and the life it has given him, or give up everything for a principle.

author: CD
premise: A boy who works at a pithead sorting coal is injured in an accident. The mine owner offers his mother five pounds to sign a paper. A young chapel preacher advises her not to sign, and the owner's agent threatens to evict the family.

author: CD
premise: A street performer who exhibits a learned pig loses the pig to a rival through a card game. He enlists the help of a hot-pie man, a ballad-seller, and a girl who sells watercress to win the pig back.
setting: A fair on the outskirts of London, 1830s

author: CD
premise: A cheerful, improvident young couple set up house on credit, and every tradesman in the street extends it because they are so pleasant. When the bills arrive together, the husband's maiden aunt, whom they have always avoided, comes to stay and take charge.
setting: A villa in Kentish Town, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: An undertaker's mute, hired to stand at funerals looking sorrowful, is mistaken for a grieving relative at a rich man's funeral, and invited to the reading of the will. He is too frightened to correct the mistake.
setting: A churchyard and a house in Kensington, London, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A young English governess employed by a French family is arrested with them when they try to flee Paris. In prison she is the only one who knows how to cook, wash, or mend, and the proud family slowly comes to depend on her.

author: CD
premise: A ferryman's daughter on the Thames estuary is courted by a customs officer and by a smuggler whose boat the officer is trying to catch. Her father wants a quiet life. On a foggy night, both men need her father's ferry.

author: CD
premise: A self-important parish constable takes lodgings with a widow who keeps a cookshop, intending to marry her for her savings. She intends to marry him for the respectability of his office. Each discovers the other's motive on the wedding morning.

author: CD
premise: A young man returns to his native village after making a fortune in Australia and finds his old friends either dead or ashamed of him. Only the village schoolmistress, who taught him to read, receives him as he was.

author: CD
premise: A travelling theatre company stranded in a manufacturing town by a broken axle puts on a play to pay for repairs. The mill owner forbids his hands to attend. The play the company chooses is about a cruel mill owner.

author: CD
premise: An English sea captain smuggling refugees out of France is asked to carry a child whose parents have been arrested. The child's nurse insists on coming. The captain suspects the nurse is a spy for the revolutionary committee.

author: CD
premise: A young man working as a clerk for a firm of solicitors is asked to deliver a packet to a lady in a great house. She receives it without opening it, and asks him to call again. He returns every week for a year without learning what the packet contained.
setting: London and a great house in Essex, 1840s

author: CD
premise: A fire destroys a mill in a manufacturing town, throwing three hundred hands out of work. The owner, insured, plans to rebuild elsewhere. A foreman who saved the ledgers from the fire discovers that the insurance was taken out only a week before.

author: GE
premise: A newly appointed vicar in a provincial town proposes to found a lending library for working men. The town's leading manufacturer supports him for reasons of his own, the old curate opposes him from habit, and the vicar slowly discovers that every gift in the town comes with an obligation attached.

author: GE
premise: A village wheelwright, respected for his honesty, is asked by the squire's steward to value a neighbour's cart for a debt seizure. He knows the true value will ruin the neighbour, and that a lower figure would be a lie. The whole village waits to see what he will say.

author: GE
premise: A brother and sister who have run their late father's draper's shop together for ten years quarrel when the brother wishes to marry a woman the sister thinks shallow. The shop cannot support two households. Each believes the other's happiness depends on their own sacrifice.

author: GE
premise: A tanner's son, apprenticed to a London bookseller, returns home for his father's funeral and finds the yard sold and his mother living on a cousin's charity. He has a small salary and a large ambition, and must decide which of them to sacrifice.
setting: A market town on the Trent, 1820s

author: GE
premise: A young barrister of independent means, who has never needed to work, takes up the case of a poor glove-maker accused of theft. The case teaches him how little he knows of the town in which he grew up, and how comfortable his ignorance has been.

author: GE
premise: An election in a county town divides a family: the father, a brewer, supports the old member who drinks his beer; the son supports a reformer who promises the vote to men like the brewer's own workers. Their quarrel spills into the brewery yard.
setting: A county town during the Reform agitation, 1832

author: GE
premise: A young widow with a small fortune is pursued by a charming fortune hunter whom her friends warn her against. She marries him to prove her independence of judgement. Within a year she must decide whether to admit her friends were right.

author: GE
premise: A curate's wife, educated above her station, finds the parish ladies condescending and the parish poor suspicious. When her husband is passed over for a living in favour of a dull man with connections, she must decide whether her ambition has harmed him.

author: GE
premise: A stonemason working on the restoration of a village church refuses to carve a memorial praising a dead squire whom he knew to be a cruel landlord. The squire's widow is paying. The vicar asks the mason whether truth belongs on gravestones.

author: GE
premise: A widow who has sacrificed everything for her only son discovers that he has secretly married a girl from the chapel she despises. He asks her blessing. She must weigh her love for him against her bitterness at being deceived.
setting: A market town in the Midlands, 1840s

author: GE
premise: A young woman of good family who wishes to study medicine is forbidden by her guardian and mocked by her suitors. A cousin who admires her offers to marry her and support her studies, but she suspects he wants her gratitude more than her freedom.

author: GE
premise: A respectable spinster who has lent money to half the town is found to be nearly ruined by a bad investment. Her debtors, relieved of their obligations by her silence, must decide whether to repay her now that she needs it.
setting: A cathedral town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A shepherd who has worked forty years on the same farm is told by the new tenant that he is too old. The shepherd's grandson, a quick boy who has learned to read, writes a letter on his behalf to the landlord, who has never visited the farm.

author: GE
premise: A German music teacher settled in an English provincial town is suspected by the parents of his pupils of radical opinions. When a pupil's father, a magistrate, demands he sign a declaration of loyalty, he must choose between his living and his self-respect.

author: GE
premise: A pious draper who sits on the board of the town's charity school discovers that its master beats the children. The master is the son of the minister to whom the draper owes his position in the chapel. He must decide whether to speak.

author: GE
premise: A young woman who sells eggs and cheese at the market is courted by a well-to-do grazier and a poor but clever stone-mason. Her mother favours the grazier. The girl's choice is complicated by a promise she made to the mason before the grazier's interest became known.

author: GE
premise: A boy who has always been his father's favourite is accused at school of cheating, and his elder sister, who knows he is guilty, is asked by their father to speak for his character. Her loyalty to her brother and her truthfulness cannot both survive.

author: GE
premise: A brilliant young man who has failed to win a university prize resolves to abandon scholarship for a life of travel. His guardian, who sacrificed much to educate him, receives the news without reproach, and the young man finds that silence harder than anger.

author: GE
premise: An elderly clergyman, kind and absent-minded, has been deceived for years by a curate who keeps the parish accounts. A young lady who visits the poor discovers the fraud. She must decide whether to tell the old man, knowing it will break his heart.

author: GE
premise: An old weaver's cottage is wanted by the new railway company. The weaver refuses to sell. His neighbours, who have been offered good prices, begin to resent his stubbornness, and the parson is asked to persuade him.

author: GE
premise: A celebrated actress who has retired to marry a nobleman finds the life of a country house intolerable. When an old manager invites her back to the stage for a single season, she must weigh her husband's honour against the only work that ever made her feel alive.

author: GE
premise: A young man who has always been expected to take orders loses his faith while preparing for his ordination. His family's income depends on the living he is to receive. He must tell his mother, who has prayed for this day for twenty years.
setting: A provincial town and a nearby rectory, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A village carrier who drives to market twice a week becomes the confidant of everyone on his route. When a girl asks him to carry a letter in secret, he must decide whether he is a man of business who carries what he is paid to carry, or a man with a conscience.

author: GE
premise: An heiress who has been raised to believe her fortune entitles her to admiration loses it in a bank failure. Her suitors fall away. A governess position is the only offer she receives, and she must decide whether pride or necessity will govern her.

author: GE
premise: A scientific gentleman who collects fossils is ridiculed by the town for his eccentricity. When a quarry owner finds a remarkable specimen, the gentleman must decide whether to buy it with money he has set aside for his daughter's marriage.
setting: A Midlands town near limestone quarries, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A farmer's son who has been away as a soldier returns to find his sweetheart married to his brother. He takes work on the farm as a labourer and lives in the same house. All three must find a way to live together that does not end in ruin.
setting: A farm in Derbyshire after the wars, 1816

author: GE
premise: A young man who has inherited his father's debts and his father's good name must choose between selling the family land to pay creditors and asking his rich uncle for a loan. The uncle has always regarded his father as a fool.

author: GE
premise: A painter of modest reputation is commissioned to paint the portrait of a powerful statesman's wife. In the sittings, she speaks to him with a frankness she shows no one else. He must decide whether to paint what he sees or what her husband expects.

author: GE
premise: A respectable doctor's widow takes in a lodger, a mysterious foreign gentleman who pays well and keeps strange hours. The town's gossip fastens on the household. The widow's daughter, who has nothing else to do, begins to investigate the lodger herself.
setting: A provincial town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A woman who keeps the village alehouse is the only person who knows that the respected churchwarden drinks in secret. When the churchwarden leads a campaign to close the alehouse, she must decide whether to reveal what she knows.

author: GE
premise: A young woman nursing her sick mother is visited daily by the doctor's assistant, a clever, poor young man. Her family assume she will marry the prosperous neighbour who has courted her for years. She must decide how much to let herself feel before the mother recovers or dies.

author: GE
premise: An earnest young clergyman who dreams of reform is offered a fashionable London living by a wealthy patron who expects him to preach comfortable sermons. A poor parish in the north has also offered him its living.
setting: London and the north of England, 1860s

author: GE
premise: A cheerful auctioneer who knows everyone's business is asked to sell the effects of an old family fallen on hard times. Among the lots is a packet of letters that would ruin a respected man. He must decide whether to sell, burn, or return them.
setting: A market town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A labourer's widow who has always been too proud to accept parish relief falls ill in winter. The rector's wife, who has quarrelled with her, is the only person who notices. Their reconciliation over the sickbed is grudging and complete.

author: GE
premise: A young man has promised his dying mother that he will look after his weak-minded brother. When an opportunity arrives to emigrate to Canada and make his fortune, the brother cannot come. He must decide whether a promise to the dead binds the living.

author: GE
premise: A woman who has written a successful novel under a male name is invited to a literary dinner by a critic who praised it. She attends as the author's sister. Over dinner, the critic tells her what he really thinks of women who write.

author: GE
premise: A new schoolmaster in a provincial town replaces rote learning with lessons in natural history. The parents complain that their sons learn nothing useful, and the trustees threaten to dismiss him. A solitary boy who has begun collecting beetles is his only defender.

author: GE
premise: A young woman who has been in service in a great house returns to her parents' cottage with fine manners and a secret. Her mother sees she is unhappy. Her father wants her to marry the blacksmith, who has waited for her for three years.

author: GE
premise: A girl of sixteen whose father has failed in business is sent to keep house for a bachelor uncle, a dry and silent lawyer. She expects to be miserable. Over a winter she finds that the uncle reads poetry in secret and has been unhappy for thirty years.
setting: A cathedral town in the Midlands, 1820s

author: GE
premise: A young diplomat returning from abroad to inherit an estate finds his fiancée has broken their engagement to devote herself to nursing. He thinks her decision a whim. She asks him to visit the hospital before he judges.

author: GE
premise: A town is building a new chapel, and two families who have long been rivals both wish to lay the foundation stone. The minister, who owes his place to one family and his conscience to the other, must decide.
setting: A manufacturing town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A farmer who has never been able to read is elected overseer of the poor. He must keep accounts he cannot check. His daughter offers to keep them for him, and soon discovers that the previous overseer stole from the poor rate.

author: GE
premise: A wealthy philanthropist decides to build model cottages for labourers and hires a young architect with advanced ideas. The labourers prefer their old cottages. The philanthropist's wife thinks her husband vain. The architect must satisfy them all.

author: GE
premise: A widow who keeps a respectable school for young ladies learns that one of her pupils has eloped with a music master. She must face the girl's father, a powerful manufacturer, and defend her school's reputation.
setting: A provincial town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: GE
premise: A young curate falls ill in a remote parish, and is nursed by a farmer's family. The farmer's daughter, who has never left the village, finds herself drawn to the books he lends her, and to him.

author: GE
premise: A gentleman who has spent his fortune on travel and pleasure returns to England to find that his cousin, a quiet woman he once dismissed, has become a respected writer on social questions. He seeks her out, unsure whether he wants her pity or her respect.

author: GE
premise: A young man of humble birth who has risen to become a bank clerk is courted by the manager's daughter, who wishes to escape her father. He is flattered. His mother, who keeps a small shop, warns him that he is being used.

author: GE
premise: A young farm labourer who has taught himself to read becomes the leader of a reading society that meets in a barn. The farmer who owns the barn is willing until the society begins to read newspapers. The labourer must choose between his patron and his friends.

author: GE
premise: A daughter discovers that her mother, long believed a widow, was in fact deserted by a husband who still lives. The father writes asking to meet his daughter before he dies. Her mother forbids it.

author: GE
premise: A young woman married to a kind but limited country squire discovers in the first year that he will never share her interest in books or ideas. She must decide whether to cultivate her mind alone or to give up the effort for the sake of peace.
setting: A country house in the Midlands, 1830s

author: HGW
premise: A chemist lodging at a seaside inn out of season experiments with a compound that makes ordinary plants grow at an astonishing rate. Within a week the inn's garden is a jungle, the landlady is frightened, and the village constable begins asking questions the chemist cannot answer.

author: HGW
premise: A suburban insurance clerk wakes to find that the river has risen overnight and the trains have stopped. Over three days he and his neighbours watch their orderly world give way as the water climbs and nobody in authority seems to know what to do.

author: HGW
premise: A girl of nineteen who has passed the matriculation examination with distinction is told by her widowed mother that the family cannot afford further study and that she must take a position as a shop cashier. Her older brother's fees, meanwhile, are being paid. She confronts her mother at the dinner table.

author: HGW
premise: A naturalist on an expedition to a remote atoll finds a species of crab that appears to cooperate in ways no crab should. His companion, a ship's mate, wants to collect them for sale. The naturalist begins to suspect the crabs are studying the men.
setting: An atoll in the South Pacific, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A country doctor's assistant who has developed a serum that suppresses fatigue begins taking it himself. He works through night after night, and his practice flourishes, until his patients notice that he no longer seems quite human.

author: HGW
premise: A young science teacher at a private school is dismissed for teaching evolution to the boys. He takes a post as a crammer, preparing dull young men for army examinations. A student's sister, who has read all the books he admires, begins to visit the classroom.

author: HGW
premise: An engineer sent to inspect a mine in the Andes finds that the mine's owner, a reclusive scientist, has been breeding a strain of fungus that consumes rock. The fungus is spreading. The owner wants the engineer to help him keep it secret.
setting: A mine in the high Andes, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A future world government has eliminated poverty by assigning every citizen a ration of goods. A clerk in the rationing bureau notices that the figures for his district do not add up, and that someone is quietly feeding thousands of people who do not officially exist.

author: HGW
premise: A wave of an unknown illness spreads through London. The authorities deny it, the newspapers dramatise it, and a clerk in the Board of Health, who has seen the figures, must decide whether to take them to a journalist.

author: HGW
premise: A young woman who has trained as a pharmacist is refused registration because of her sex. She takes work as an unofficial assistant to a dispensing chemist who passes off her work as his own. When a patient is nearly poisoned by the chemist's error, she must decide whether to reveal who actually mixed the medicines.

author: HGW
premise: An amateur meteorologist in a country village predicts a great storm from his homemade instruments and is ridiculed by the parish council. When the storm arrives, his cellar becomes the only refuge in the village, and he must decide whether to let in the councillors who mocked him.

author: HGW
premise: A man who invents a machine that can see events at a distance discovers that it shows him not the present but the future. He sees a war that will destroy his country, and nobody will believe him.

author: HGW
premise: An earthquake strikes the south of England without warning. A shop assistant and a young lady who has never done anything for herself are trapped together in a collapsed tea room, and must dig their way out.

author: HGW
premise: A professor who has discovered a substance that cancels the effect of gravity tests it on a garden chair. The chair floats away. The professor's housekeeper, who sat on it, is carried over the rooftops of a quiet town.
setting: A university town in the Midlands, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A doctor on a remote trading station in Africa is visited by an English scientist who wishes to study a local disease that confers immunity to pain. The scientist's methods trouble the doctor, who begins to fear for the villagers.
setting: A trading station on the West African coast, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A traveller from the present awakens in a future England where everyone lives to two hundred and nobody has children any longer. The elderly population is serene and slowly dwindling. He meets the last child born, now a lonely woman of thirty.

author: HGW
premise: A young man from the lower middle classes wins a scholarship to a technical college and meets students of every class. He is ashamed of his origins and ashamed of his shame. When his father visits the college, he must decide whether to acknowledge him.

author: HGW
premise: A photographer's new lens reveals, in every portrait he takes, faint shapes standing behind his sitters. His customers are delighted with the novelty. He alone suspects the shapes are real and are coming closer.

author: HGW
premise: A great city of the future has abolished night with artificial suns. A young woman who works in the lighting office discovers that the system is failing, and that the city's people have forgotten how to live in the dark.

author: HGW
premise: Every motor car in England stops working on the same day. A provincial motor-dealer who has staked his fortune on the new machines must decide whether to flee his creditors or help his neighbours walk to the nearest town.

author: HGW
premise: A middle-aged schoolmistress who has spent twenty years teaching the daughters of the wealthy decides to open a school for the daughters of shopkeepers. Her former employers are scandalised, and the shopkeepers suspect her of condescension.

author: HGW
premise: A young engineer builds a flying machine in a barn and offers rides to the villagers. The vicar preaches against it, the squire wants to buy it, and the girl the engineer admires is the first to volunteer to fly.
setting: A village on the South Downs, 1900s

author: HGW
premise: A ship's doctor stranded on a whaling station in the far south discovers in the ice the frozen body of an animal unknown to science. The station manager wants to sell it. The doctor realises that it is beginning to thaw.
setting: A whaling station in the Southern Ocean, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: In a future where disease has been abolished, a young man becomes the first person in a century to fall ill. The society, which has no doctors and no hospitals, does not know how to treat him, and fears him.

author: HGW
premise: A meteorite shower sets fire to the moors above a northern manufacturing town. The mill hands are sent to fight the fires. A young striker who has been blacklisted takes command, and the mill owner must decide whether to follow him.

author: HGW
premise: A young wife whose husband is a successful but dull estate agent joins a society for the discussion of advanced ideas. Her husband is first amused, then alarmed. When she announces she wishes to earn her own money, he goes to her father for help.

author: HGW
premise: An explorer returns from the Amazon with a captive plant that feeds on insects, and gives it to his old tutor as a gift. The tutor tends it with growing devotion. His housekeeper notices that the plant has begun to need larger meals.
setting: A house in Hampstead, with a past in the Amazon, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A traveller in a future world is taken for a ghost by a people who have never seen a man with grey hair. Their society has found a way to halt ageing at thirty, and they regard his age as a deformity. He tries to explain the dignity of growing old.
setting: A city in the far future

author: HGW
premise: A new strain of wheat, bred to grow in poor soil, spreads beyond the experimental farm where it was developed and begins to choke out every other crop in the county. The scientist who bred it must face the farmers whose fields are being overrun.

author: HGW
premise: A self-made manufacturer of a patent tonic, who has grown rich on advertising, decides to stand for Parliament. His nephew, who helped him build the business, is ashamed of the tonic and admires the uncle anyway.

author: HGW
premise: A physicist who has learned to slow the passage of time within a small room offers to let his landlady use it to finish her washing in a minute. She agrees, and begins to suspect that he has other uses for it.

author: HGW
premise: A lighthouse keeper on a remote island sees a creature rise from the sea at night. He reports it, and a naturalist arrives with a camera and a rifle. The keeper begins to feel protective of the creature.
setting: A lighthouse in the Outer Hebrides, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A great fog descends on London and does not lift for a month. Trade stops, crime rises, and a group of Socialists in a cellar debate whether to seize the moment. A timid bank clerk who has wandered in by mistake finds himself elected their secretary.

author: HGW
premise: A young man who has failed his examinations takes a post as assistant in a chemist's shop in a seaside town. He falls in love with a holiday visitor above his station, and pretends to be a medical student. Her brother comes to the shop.

author: HGW
premise: An eccentric inventor of a machine that translates the speech of animals tests it on his neighbour's dog, and learns that the dog has a great deal to say about its owner. The neighbour sues.

author: HGW
premise: A colonial official on a remote island discovers that the islanders have a medicine that reverses ageing. A company in London wants the formula. The official must decide whether to betray the islanders or his employers.

author: HGW
premise: A young woman of the future, raised in a world without war, discovers in an archive the records of the last great battle. She becomes obsessed with understanding why people once fought, and begins to see the possibility of war in her own gentle society.
setting: An archive city in the far future

author: HGW
premise: The sun dims by a fraction, and winter does not end. A farmer in the Weald, practical and sceptical, organises his neighbours to grow food under glass, while the government in London insists the problem is temporary.

author: HGW
premise: A woman who has worked as a typist for ten years is engaged to a kindly older man who expects her to give up her work. She loves the independence of her small wage and her lodgings. On the eve of the wedding she visits the office one last time.

author: HGW
premise: A young scientist discovers that a common weed contains a substance that makes people briefly incapable of lying. He tests it at a dinner party given by his ambitious aunt. The results are catastrophic for her social position.

author: HGW
premise: A missionary's son, raised in a remote mountain valley, returns to England for his education. He is terrified by the noise of London and fascinated by its machines. He writes letters to his father describing English customs as if they were those of savages.
setting: London, with a past in a mountain valley, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A sudden shortage of coal brings industrial England to a halt. A coal merchant who has hoarded his stock is offered a fortune by the government and a beating by his neighbours. His daughter, a socialist, tells him what she thinks.

author: HGW
premise: An ironmonger's son who wants to be an artist is apprenticed to his father's trade instead. He paints in secret in the attic. When a London dealer sees one of his pictures in a pub, he must choose between his father's shop and an uncertain life.
setting: A market town in Kent and London, 1890s

author: HGW
premise: A traveller visits a future city where every citizen is assigned a profession at birth by a machine that measures their aptitudes. He meets a woman assigned to be a sweeper who wishes to be a poet.

author: HGW
premise: An outbreak of madness among the horses of London makes the streets impassable. A cab driver who has always loved his horse refuses to have it shot, and hides it in a basement while the city falls into chaos above.

author: HGW
premise: A widow who keeps a boarding house for clerks finds herself the confidante of all her lodgers. When two of them fall in love with the same typist, and a third is arrested for embezzlement, she must hold her household together.
setting: A boarding house in Clapham, London, 1900s

author: HGW
premise: A lecturer in physics accidentally creates a tiny pocket of space where the laws of nature are reversed. He keeps it in a glass jar in his rooms, and his landlady, cleaning, knocks it over.

author: HGW
premise: A cheerful bicycling clerk on his annual holiday encounters a young woman who has run away from her guardian. He offers to escort her through the country lanes to her aunt's. Her guardian, in pursuit, believes the worst of both.

author: HGW
premise: A palaeontologist digging in a remote desert finds the remains of a creature that walked upright before humanity existed. Beside the bones are tools. His expedition's sponsor wants the find kept quiet.

author: HGW
premise: A rumour spreads through England that a meteor will strike the earth at midnight. A respectable family in a cathedral city spends the evening confessing its secrets to one another. The meteor misses.
setting: A cathedral city in the south of England, 1900s

author: JA
premise: A widowed baronet's second daughter is courted simultaneously by a rich, tedious neighbour and a clever but poor curate. Her elder sister, who has no suitors at all, gives her advice so evidently self-interested that the younger is driven to prefer whichever man her sister dislikes.

author: JA
premise: A family accustomed to comfort learn that their father has lost a third of his income in a failed canal investment. The mother insists on keeping the carriage for appearance's sake; the eldest daughter quietly calculates how many economies would be needed to keep it, and which of her sisters will notice.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who prides herself on her judgement is asked by her godmother to choose a husband for her cousin from among three local gentlemen. She makes her choice with care, presents it with confidence, and learns that her cousin has already accepted a fourth man nobody had thought to consider.

author: JA
premise: A sensible young woman is mortified when her mother announces at a dinner party that her daughter will soon be engaged to a gentleman who has never proposed. The gentleman is present. The daughter must undo the damage without contradicting her mother in public.
setting: A house in a country town in Hertfordshire, 1800s

author: JA
premise: A country girl visiting London for the first time with a fashionable aunt is taken up by a set of fine young ladies whose friendship proves expensive. She discovers that the aunt's own reputation in town is less secure than it appeared from the country.
setting: A house in Upper Brook Street, London, 1810s

author: JA
premise: An heiress of twenty-five, who has refused several offers and is thought cold, is unexpectedly courted by her late brother's closest friend, a naval surgeon of no family. Her guardian is opposed. She must decide whether her caution has been wisdom or merely fear.

author: JA
premise: A young lady newly come into a small fortune is advised by her married sister on every particular of dress, company, and conduct. She follows the advice dutifully for a season, finds herself universally approved and thoroughly bored, and resolves to make one decision entirely on her own.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's family is visited by a wealthy cousin who means to choose a bride among the daughters. The youngest daughter, who is fifteen and outspoken, makes it her business to mock him. Her sisters are horrified; the cousin is unexpectedly charmed.

author: JA
premise: A young lady and her mother take lodgings in a spa town for the mother's health. The mother is not ill. The daughter discovers that her mother has come to renew acquaintance with a former suitor, now widowed, and is uncertain whether to be shocked or delighted.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman who has inherited an estate encumbered with debts must marry money or sell. He courts a manufacturer's daughter whose fortune would save him, and finds that she understands his situation perfectly and has terms of her own.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who believes herself above vanity is flattered by the attentions of a fashionable gentleman visiting the neighbourhood. When she learns he has been laying a wager on her affections, she must examine how much her good sense was worth.

author: JA
premise: A widow who lives in comfortable dependence on her son's estate fears that his new wife will turn her out of the house. She exhausts herself in attentions to the daughter-in-law, who wants nothing more than to be left alone with a book.

author: JA
premise: A young man of moderate means, visiting a fashionable relation in town, falls in love with a girl he believes to be an heiress. She believes him to be rich. They are both mistaken, and both too embarrassed to say so.

author: JA
premise: A young woman learns that her closest friend's brother, whom she has privately liked for some time, has lost his money at cards and is leaving for the West Indies. Her friend begs her to say nothing that might keep him in England, where his creditors wait. She must hold her tongue at the farewell dinner.

author: JA
premise: A young man about to enter the church is offered a better living by a patron on condition that he marry the patron's plain niece. He has an understanding with a girl of no fortune. His mother urges prudence. He must choose between the living and the girl.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's wife who delights in arranging her parishioners' lives promotes a match between the village doctor and the squire's niece. Both are polite to her and to each other. Neither has the slightest wish to marry, and they unite only in their efforts to escape her kindness.

author: JA
premise: A naval officer on shore leave escorts his sister to Bath, where she meets a gentleman he despises. He must decide whether to forbid the acquaintance, knowing that his sister is of age and he has no right to command her.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who has been engaged for two years to a man waiting for preferment begins to doubt that she loves him. He is good, dull, and devoted. She must decide whether to break the engagement and face her family's displeasure.

author: JA
premise: Two sisters inherit a small house and an annuity from their godmother. The elder wishes to live quietly; the younger wishes to spend the annuity on a season in London. Their brother, who expected the inheritance himself, offers to mediate.

author: JA
premise: A young lady who takes pride in her frankness offends the neighbourhood by speaking her mind about a newly married couple. She discovers too late that the bride is the sister of the man she most wishes to please.

author: JA
premise: A mother whose ambition is to see her daughters married to titles takes them to a resort where a young lord is said to be staying. The lord proves to be an awkward boy of seventeen with a governess. The daughters must disguise their mother's disappointment from the whole resort.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's daughter staying with a rich friend in London is taken to a fashionable assembly where she knows no one. She is rescued from solitude by an amusing elderly gentleman, and finds she has spent the evening talking to the father of the man she came to London hoping to avoid.

author: JA
premise: A rich old gentleman, tired of his relations' attentions, announces that he will leave his fortune to a charity. His relations are devastated. His young ward, who never wanted the fortune, is the only one who visits him in the following month.

author: JA
premise: A young man who believes himself too clever to be deceived is taken in by a charming young lady who flatters his opinions. His sister, who sees through her at once, must decide whether to warn him and risk his resentment.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman of consequence is mortified when his younger brother, a cheerful sea officer, arrives unexpectedly at a formal dinner, tells stories of shipwreck, and proposes to the eldest daughter of the house before the dessert.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who has always laughed at her elder brother's choice of friends finds that the one she mocked most has become a respected magistrate and is now courting her particular friend. She must decide whether to confess to her friend everything she has said of him.

author: JA
premise: A family of daughters is thrown into consternation by the arrival of a letter from their father's long-estranged brother, who has made a fortune abroad and proposes to visit. No one remembers what the quarrel was about, and each sister has a different theory about what he will want.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's father, a kindly but absent-minded scholar, invites a gentleman to dinner and forgets to tell his wife. The household has nothing in the larder. The daughter must manage the evening without letting the guest suspect.

author: JA
premise: Two sisters are invited to stay with a cousin who has married into a great family. They are treated as poor relations. The younger sister is resentful; the elder observes that the cousin is not happy either.
