author: JA
premise: A young woman agrees to marry an older man for his kindness and his estate, and on the eve of her wedding meets his nephew, who is everything she had once hoped for. She does not break her promise. The nephew does not ask her to.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman's only son returns from university with debts his father cannot pay. The father proposes to sell the family's best timber. His wife proposes the son marry an heiress. The son proposes nothing, and goes shooting.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who is certain that a neighbour's governess is designing to marry her employer sets out to protect him. The governess has no such design. The employer, however, has.

author: JA
premise: A family's eldest son marries a woman of fashion who despises his family's country manners. She arrives for her first visit determined to reform them. The family, determined not to be reformed, close ranks with exquisite politeness.

author: JA
premise: A young lady staying in London for the season is introduced to a gentleman whose name she recognises as that of a man her brother quarrelled with years before. She does not know the cause of the quarrel. He clearly does.

author: JA
premise: A rich young man and a poor young woman, who have been meeting secretly in a shrubbery, are discovered by her aunt. The aunt, rather than forbid the match, insists on managing it, and very nearly ruins it.

author: JA
premise: A widow with three daughters and a small jointure is courted by a wealthy merchant who has made his fortune in trade. Her neighbours think the match degrading. Her daughters think it sensible. She thinks only that he is the first man to make her laugh in years.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who believes her elder sister incapable of strong feeling is astonished to discover a packet of love letters in her sister's drawer. She must decide whether to confess what she has seen, and what she now knows of her sister.

author: JA
premise: A country clergyman visits London to petition a bishop, and is entertained by a fashionable cousin who regards him as a curiosity. His good sense and simplicity, mocked at first, begin to win the regard of the cousin's guests.

author: JA
premise: An officer of the militia, quartered in a small town, is courted by every mother with a daughter. He prefers the one young woman who seems indifferent to him, and cannot understand why his charm fails with her.

author: JA
premise: A mother who fancies herself an invalid summons her married daughter home in a crisis that proves to be a cold. The daughter's husband, who has come too, is so patient with his mother-in-law that his wife begins to suspect he enjoys it.

author: JA
premise: Two young women from a country parish attend their first public ball at a resort town. One dances every dance; the other dances none. The one who dances none is the one who receives a call the next morning.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's sister has been courted for two years by a gentleman who will not declare himself. The younger sister, impatient, resolves to make him speak. Her methods are ingenious, and very nearly drive him away.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman of good family but small income is pressed by his sisters to marry a rich widow they have chosen for him. He likes the widow and dislikes being managed. He must decide whether to marry her in spite of his sisters or refuse her because of them.

author: JA
premise: A young woman convinced that her new sister-in-law is a fortune hunter watches her closely for proof. The sister-in-law, aware of the scrutiny, behaves with perfect propriety, which only confirms the young woman's suspicion.

author: JA
premise: A family's plans for a picnic are overturned when their eccentric great-aunt insists on coming and bringing her parrot. The parrot's conversation, learned from a sea captain, makes a certain impression on the gentleman the eldest daughter hopes to impress.

author: JA
premise: A young lady staying with friends in a fashionable town is warned against a gentleman with a dangerous reputation. She finds him serious, kind, and dull. Her friends cannot account for her disappointment.

author: JA
premise: A young clergyman who has always admired a neighbour's daughter at a distance is asked by her father to advise her on her reading. Their lessons are conducted with perfect propriety, and neither of them has ever been more uncomfortable.

author: JA
premise: A young heiress is warned by her guardian that every man who courts her wants only her money. She resolves to test her suitors by pretending to have lost her fortune. Only one remains, and he is the one she likes least.

author: JA
premise: A young woman of strong opinions refuses to meet her brother's fiancée, having decided from report that she is frivolous. When illness obliges them to nurse the brother together, she discovers the fiancée's patience and her own prejudice.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's younger brother, newly returned from school, falls violently in love with a governess at a neighbouring house. His family is horrified; his sister, who likes the governess, is torn between loyalty and amusement.

author: JC
premise: A young second mate, on his first voyage with the rank, freezes during a squall and the captain takes the deck in his place. Nobody speaks of it afterwards. For the rest of the passage the mate watches the crew for any sign that they saw, and the captain for any sign that he will report it.
setting: A barque in the Indian Ocean, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An English railway engineer surveying a line through the mountains of a small republic is caught between the government that hired him and a rebel general who controls the passes. Both demand his loyalty, and each promises that the railway will bring civilisation.

author: JC
premise: A police inspector who has spent years cultivating informers among London's foreign revolutionaries is ordered by a new superior to make an arrest that will please the newspapers. The only man he can plausibly arrest is the informer who has kept him safe.

author: JC
premise: A Russian student living in exile in a Swiss city is approached by a revolutionary committee who believe him to be one of them. He is not, but their trust is the only warmth he has known since leaving home. He must decide how long he can let the mistake continue.

author: JC
premise: A surveyor sent to map a river for a concession company finds that the villages marked on his predecessor's chart do not exist, and never did. The company's directors in Europe have already sold shares on the strength of the chart. He must decide what his own map will show.

author: JC
premise: A captain whose ship has gone aground through his own error must give evidence at the inquiry. His mate, who warned him, is called next. The captain watches the mate in the witness box and waits to learn whether loyalty or truth will prevail.

author: JC
premise: A Basque sea captain who carries mail along the coast of a turbulent republic is ordered by a rebel commander to land a cargo of rifles at a fishing village. He has carried every kind of cargo for thirty years and never asked what was in a crate. This time he knows.
setting: A coastal steamer off a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A Polish widow living in Paris receives a visit from a young man who claims to have shared a prison cell with her son in Warsaw. He brings the son's last message. She wants to believe him, and notices that he cannot meet her eyes.

author: JC
premise: A ship's carpenter is accused by the crew of stealing from the stores during a long calm. The captain believes him innocent but cannot prove it. As the calm continues and water runs short, the crew's suspicion hardens into something dangerous.
setting: A sailing ship becalmed in the Atlantic, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A hotel keeper in the capital of a small republic has served every president and every rebel who has ever taken a room. When two rival generals book the same floor on the same night, he must keep them from discovering each other until morning.
setting: A hotel in a South American capital, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A watchmaker in a London back street repairs timepieces for respectable customers and is asked one evening to repair a device whose purpose he guesses at once. The customer pays in advance. The watchmaker must decide whether to do the work, refuse it, or go to the police.

author: JC
premise: A Russian railway official who has always prided himself on having no politics is ordered to delay a train carrying a political prisoner, so that the prisoner's comrades may attempt a rescue. The order comes from his own brother.

author: JC
premise: A missionary and a trader share a small island station. They despise each other's work and depend on each other's company. When the trader's supply boat fails to arrive, they are left alone together for six months.
setting: An island in the Malay Archipelago, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A British consul in a small republic, who has spent twenty years writing reports nobody reads, receives a telegram announcing that a warship is coming to protect British interests. He realises he no longer knows what the British interests are, or whether he still shares them.

author: JC
premise: A Swiss pastor whose congregation includes several Russian exiles is asked by one of them to perform a marriage without asking questions. The groom gives a false name. The pastor must decide whether a sacrament can rest on a lie.

author: JC
premise: A harbour pilot who once refused to take a ship out in a storm, against the owner's demand, learns years later that the owner has become chairman of the harbour board. The pilot is summoned to the board to explain a minor delay.

author: JC
premise: A ship chandler in a port of a South American republic is entrusted by the departing English consul with the consulate's archives. When a revolutionary colonel demands them, the chandler must decide whether a few boxes of paper are worth his life.
setting: A port in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A middle-aged anarchist who has lived for years on the subscriptions of wealthy sympathisers is introduced to a young lady who wishes to give him her fortune. He realises, for the first time, that he does not believe in anything.
setting: A drawing room in Mayfair, London, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A revolutionary agent sent from Russia to assassinate a minister abroad falls ill on the journey and is nursed by a family of Swiss peasants. Their simple decency disturbs him more than any argument he has heard against his cause.
setting: A village in the Swiss Alps, 1900s

author: JC
premise: A ship's master falls ill on a long voyage, and the first mate takes command. When the master recovers and wishes to resume command, the mate, who has proved a better seaman, must decide whether to surrender it.
setting: A clipper in the South Atlantic, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A general who has seized power in a small republic invites the foreign merchants to a banquet to reassure them. A young lieutenant of his guard, who has seen what happened in the provinces, serves the wine and listens.
setting: A presidential palace in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A young typist employed by a revolutionary journal in London discovers that its editor is in the pay of a foreign police. She must decide whether to expose him and destroy the journal she believes in, or keep silent and keep her place.
setting: A printing office in Islington, London, 1900s

author: JC
premise: A Russian countess living in a Swiss pension is visited by her husband's former secretary, who announces that he has joined the revolutionaries and wishes her to finance them. She has no sympathy with the revolution and a great deal for him.

author: JC
premise: A shipwrecked crew in an open boat must decide whether to make for the nearest land, where natives are reported hostile, or a distant port. The captain, who is dying, will not decide. The mate and the bosun cannot agree.
setting: An open boat in the Java Sea, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An English engineer's wife living on a coffee estate in the hills of a South American republic befriends the local priest, the only educated man within fifty miles. When revolution reaches the valley, her husband forbids the priest the house.
setting: A coffee estate in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A Russian student accused by the exiles of being a police spy must prove his innocence to a committee that has already decided his guilt. The only witness who could clear him is the man who denounced him.

author: JC
premise: A company agent at an upriver station receives orders to abandon it and return to the coast. The local chief who has protected the station begs him to stay. The agent, who has grown attached to the place, must decide whose orders he will follow.
setting: An upriver station in Central Africa, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A captain discovers that his chief officer has been secretly drinking, and that the ship's course has been wrongly reckoned for a week. Reporting the officer will ruin him. Not reporting him may lose the ship.
setting: A steamer in the Red Sea, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A young engineer working on a harbour scheme in a South American port falls in love with the daughter of a local politician. When her father joins a revolt, the engineer must decide whether to stay in the port or take the last steamer home.
setting: A port city in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A respectable bookseller in a quiet London street keeps a back room where foreign exiles meet. His wife has always pretended not to know. When the police come to the shop, she discovers how much she does know.

author: JC
premise: A seaman who gave false evidence at an inquiry to protect his captain finds, years later, that the captain has died and left him a small legacy in gratitude. He must decide whether he can accept money that feels like payment for a lie.

author: JC
premise: A fisherman's widow on a coast of a turbulent republic finds a drowned soldier on the beach with a satchel of letters. Some are addressed to the government, some to the rebels. She cannot read, and must decide whom to trust to read them for her.
setting: A fishing village on a South American coast, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A cabinet minister's private secretary is approached by an old school friend, now an anarchist, who asks for a meeting with the minister. The secretary agrees, believing he can bring about reconciliation. The friend has other intentions.

author: JC
premise: A young Russian translator employed by a Swiss publishing house is asked to translate the memoirs of a revolutionary who denounces the translator's late father as a police agent. He does not know whether the accusation is true.

author: JC
premise: A ship's boy who survived a wreck in which the captain went down with the ship is asked by the captain's widow to tell her how her husband died. The boy knows the captain died a coward. He must decide what to tell her.

author: JC
premise: A customs officer in a South American port is offered a fortune to look away while a ship is loaded at night. He has been honest all his life and poor all his life. His wife is ill, and the ship sails at dawn.

author: JC
premise: A young woman whose brother has been arrested as an anarchist goes to the police to plead for him, and finds the inspector both courteous and immovable. She returns the next day, and the next. Something in her persistence troubles the inspector.

author: JC
premise: An exile in Geneva receives a letter from his mother in Russia, begging him to return and accept the Tsar's pardon. The revolutionaries regard such letters as police tricks. He does not know whether his mother wrote it.

author: JC
premise: A priest in a mountain village of a South American republic hides the treasure of his church from a revolutionary army. The colonel who comes to find it was once his altar boy.
setting: A mountain village in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A doctor who treats the poor of the East End is consulted secretly by an anarchist who has been injured making a bomb. The doctor's oath obliges him to treat the man. His conscience demands that he inform the police.

author: JC
premise: A Russian girl who has come to Switzerland to study medicine is drawn into the circle of the exiles by a charismatic speaker. Her fellow student, a quiet Pole, warns her against him. She suspects the warning is jealousy.

author: JC
premise: A harbour master in a small Eastern port is ordered by the colonial government to refuse entry to a ship flying no flag. Its captain sends ashore a letter in a hand the harbour master recognises: his own brother's, whom he has not seen in twenty years.
setting: A port in the Dutch East Indies, 1890s

author: JC
premise: An old sea captain who has lost his sight hides it from his owners and his crew, relying on his mate to read the instruments for him. The mate is ambitious, and the owners are suspicious.
setting: A coasting steamer in the Gulf of Siam, 1880s

author: JC
premise: A newspaper editor in the capital of a small republic writes an article praising a revolt. The revolt fails. He must decide whether to flee, recant, or wait for the soldiers.

author: JC
premise: A retired police informer who has lived for years on a small pension from the Home Office is recognised in a London street by a man he once betrayed, now returned from prison. The man greets him warmly and asks him to dinner.

author: JC
premise: A ship's crew mutinies against a brutal captain. The second mate, who shares their hatred of the captain, must decide whether to join them or stand by the man he despises.
setting: A sailing ship in the Pacific, 1880s

author: JC
premise: An Englishwoman who runs a school for girls in a South American port is asked by a revolutionary leader to teach his daughter. She agrees, and finds herself regarded by both sides as a traitor.
setting: A port city in a South American republic, 1890s

author: JC
premise: A Russian revolutionary living in London receives orders to return to Russia and carry out an assassination. His English wife does not know what he is. On the night before he leaves, she asks him why he seems so far away.

author: JC
premise: A mining engineer who has spent years building a railway into the mountains of a republic, believing it would bring prosperity to the villages along its route, stands on the platform at the coast to watch the first train arrive. It is carrying soldiers.

author: JC
premise: A captain who has spent his life on sailing ships is given command of a steamer. He distrusts the engines and the engineers. When the engines fail in a storm, he must rely on the men he has despised.
setting: A steamer in the Bay of Biscay, 1890s

author: MS
premise: A retired naval captain who has never spoken of a mutiny he suppressed in his youth is asked by a young historian to describe it for a book. The captain refuses. The historian then produces a letter, written by a mutineer the captain hanged, that tells the story differently.
setting: A house on the Kent coast, 1830s

author: MS
premise: A young physician obsessed with discovering the cause of a wasting fever that killed his sister conducts experiments on himself in secret. As his health declines, his betrothed begs him to stop. He believes he is on the edge of a discovery that will save thousands.

author: MS
premise: In a future England governed as a republic, a young statesman who has dedicated his life to the public good is told that a famine in the colonies will reach the home country within a year. His colleagues prefer to hope it will not. He must decide whether to tell the people.
setting: London, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young widow whose husband drowned within a year of their marriage retires to a cottage by the sea. She refuses all company. A shy neighbour, a girl of fifteen who also lost a parent to the sea, begins leaving wild flowers at her door.
setting: A cottage on the Devon coast, 1820s

author: MS
premise: A girl taken in as a ward by a wealthy family is treated as a daughter until the family's own son falls in love with her. The mother, who had planned a grander match, begins to remind the girl gently and constantly of how much she owes them.

author: MS
premise: A young Sicilian fisherman rescues a nobleman's son from a storm at sea and is rewarded with a place in the nobleman's household. He rises in favour, and the nobleman's steward, who has served thirty years, sets out to ruin him.
setting: A palace and fishing village in Sicily, 1790s

author: MS
premise: A small community survives in the ruins of a great city after a pestilence. Its leader, a former soldier, wishes to rebuild; his rival, a former priest, believes the pestilence was a judgement and that rebuilding is blasphemy. The young people of the community must choose between them.
setting: The ruins of a European city, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: An astronomer who has devoted his life to mapping the heavens loses his sight. His daughter, who has assisted him for years, offers to continue the work. He refuses to believe a woman capable of it, and she must prove him wrong without breaking his heart.
setting: An observatory on a hill in Surrey, 1810s

author: MS
premise: A young man falsely accused of a crime committed by his father is tried and acquitted, but his reputation is ruined. His father, who could clear him, remains silent. The son must decide whether to expose his father or bear the shame himself.
setting: An assize town in the north of England, 1820s

author: MS
premise: In a future age when all nations are at peace, a sudden failure of the harvests across Europe tests the bonds between them. An English envoy sent to a congress in Vienna must persuade the nations to share their reserves, while his own countrymen demand that England keep everything.
setting: Vienna, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young chemist who believes he can restore memory to the old by a tincture of his own devising tests it on his grandfather, who has forgotten everyone. The old man remembers, and among the things he remembers is a crime that the family has kept hidden for forty years.

author: MS
premise: A widow who keeps a respectable lodging house is visited by a stranger who knows that she was once married under another name, to a man who was transported for forgery. He asks for money. She must decide whether her present life is worth what he demands.

author: MS
premise: A young woman of the future, born into a world depopulated by disease, sets out on foot across England to find her brother, from whom she has had no word for a year. Along the empty roads she meets other wanderers, each carrying a grief she recognises.
setting: England, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young heiress whose father was killed in a duel learns that the man who killed him is now a respected member of Parliament, and is about to marry her closest friend. She has proof of the duel. She must decide whether to speak.

author: MS
premise: A naturalist sails to Iceland to study its volcanoes, accompanied by his young wife, who has insisted on coming. On the voyage she proves the better observer. He must decide whether to put her name beside his on the paper he will read to the Royal Society.
setting: Iceland and a ship in the North Atlantic, 1810s

author: MS
premise: An English girl travelling with her family in Italy is courted by a young Italian patriot who is plotting against the Austrian rulers of his city. Her father forbids the acquaintance. When the patriot is arrested, she must decide whether to plead for him.

author: MS
premise: A popular general of a future English republic, returning victorious from a war in the East, is urged by his followers to make himself dictator. His oldest friend, a member of the assembly, must decide whether to oppose him in public and lose his friendship forever.
setting: London, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young woman who has nursed her mother through a long and terrible illness is left alone in the world at nineteen. A distant relative offers her a home. She refuses, and resolves to live by herself in her mother's cottage, though the village thinks her strange.

author: MS
premise: A man whose testimony sent his business partner to prison for a fraud he himself committed is visited, twenty years later, by the partner's daughter, who has come to ask for work as his secretary. She does not know who he is.

author: MS
premise: In a future England where a long sickness has emptied the towns, a young schoolmistress continues to ring the school bell every morning, though only three children remain. A government inspector arrives to close the school.
setting: A village in Oxfordshire, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young officer returning from the Peninsular War discovers that his late father's fortune was made in the slave trade. He is engaged to a woman of strong abolitionist views. He must decide whether to tell her before the wedding.

author: MS
premise: A mechanician who has built an automaton that plays chess is invited to exhibit it before a royal court. The automaton wins every game. Only the mechanician knows how, and the secret begins to weigh on him.

author: MS
premise: A ship carrying refugees from a stricken continent arrives at an English port. The townspeople, fearing infection, refuse to let them land. A young doctor among the townspeople argues that compassion is a duty. The town's council meets through the night.
setting: A port on the south coast of England, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A woman who abandoned her infant daughter in a foundling hospital twenty years before, to save her own reputation, is now a wealthy widow. She learns that her daughter is a seamstress in poverty. She must decide whether to claim her and expose herself.

author: MS
premise: An old man who has outlived his wife, his children, and all his friends lives alone in a decaying manor. A young tenant farmer's daughter begins to visit him, and he finds himself telling her the story of his life, which no one has ever heard.

author: MS
premise: In a future England where a sickness has emptied the cities, a band of survivors elects a young woman as their leader. She has never sought power. She must decide whether to lead them north to the coast or keep them in the valley they know.
setting: The Severn valley, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A respected judge learns that a man he sentenced to death years before was innocent. The true criminal has confessed on his deathbed. The judge must decide whether to make the truth public and ruin himself.
setting: An assize town in the west of England, 1830s

author: MS
premise: A scholar of the future, living in a world that has survived a great pestilence, writes a history of the catastrophe for those who will come after. As he writes, he realises that the pestilence has returned.
setting: An English university town, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young woman's guardian, a wealthy and generous man, asks her to marry him. She is grateful and fond of him. On the eve of her decision, she learns that he was once engaged to her mother and that her mother broke the engagement for her father.

author: MS
premise: A gifted young man who wishes to become a great poet is told by a famous critic that his work has no merit. He burns his manuscripts and resolves to become a man of science instead. His sister, who has kept copies of his poems, does not tell him.

author: MS
premise: A young man and woman, the last survivors of their village after a plague, decide to set out together to find other people. They are strangers to each other. On the road they must learn to trust each other, and to decide what they owe to the dead.
setting: The English countryside, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young man who has always believed himself the son of a poor curate learns that he is the illegitimate son of a nobleman. The nobleman, now dying, wishes to acknowledge him. The curate, who raised him, does not wish to lose him.
setting: A parsonage and a great house in Northumberland, 1830s

author: MS
premise: In a future England, a great storm destroys the harvest and the people turn against their government. A young aristocrat who has always despised politics finds himself called upon to speak for the people in Parliament.
setting: London, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: An elderly woman who has lived a life of quiet virtue in a provincial town confesses on her deathbed to her doctor that she once betrayed her closest friend to a man who ruined her. She asks the doctor to find the friend's descendants and ask their forgiveness.
setting: A provincial town in the Midlands, 1830s

author: MS
premise: A natural philosopher who has spent his life trying to prove the existence of a vital fluid in living things is challenged by a younger rival to a public demonstration. The philosopher's experiments have never quite worked. His reputation depends on this one.

author: MS
premise: A young woman of the future, a nurse in a hospital overwhelmed by a mysterious disease, falls in love with a patient who will not recover. She knows what she is doing, and does it anyway.
setting: A hospital in London, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A wealthy manufacturer who rose from poverty by cheating his first employer is now a celebrated benefactor of his town. The employer's grandson, a young schoolmaster, has been invited to give the address at the opening of the benefactor's new school.

author: MS
premise: A young woman jilted on the eve of her wedding by a man she loved shuts herself away from the world. Her younger brother, a lively boy of fourteen, refuses to let her withdraw, and drags her out to the hills each morning.
setting: A house in the Peak District, 1820s

author: MS
premise: In a future Europe where nations have dwindled after a pestilence, an English physician sails to Lisbon in search of a remedy said to have been found there. The city he finds is calm, orderly, and unwilling to share what it knows.
setting: Lisbon, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A girl raised by a reclusive man she believes to be her uncle finds a miniature portrait of a woman who looks exactly like her. He tells her the woman was his sister. The local vicar, who knew the family, tells her something else.
setting: A remote house on the Welsh coast, 1830s

author: MS
premise: A young man who has dedicated himself to the cause of liberty sails to Greece to fight in the war of independence. He finds the war squalid and the cause divided. His letters home grow darker, and his sister, who encouraged him to go, reads them with growing guilt.

author: MS
premise: A young woman in a future England, surviving alone in a village after a sickness, hears church bells ringing in the next valley. She has not heard another human sound in a year. She sets out at once, afraid of what she will find and more afraid of not going.
setting: The Cotswolds, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young woman discovers that her fiancé, whom she adores, fought a duel years ago in which he killed a man who was defending his sister's honour. The man's sister is now a governess in the house where the wedding is to take place.

author: MS
premise: A girl whose closest friend has died of consumption spends a summer writing letters to the dead friend, as if she still lived. Her mother finds the letters and fears for her daughter's mind.

author: MS
premise: In a future England, a prophet arises who claims that the pestilence is a punishment and that only his followers will be spared. A young doctor who has seen the disease up close sets out to expose him, and finds the prophet sincere.
setting: A town in the English Midlands, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A respected banker discovers that his wife, before their marriage, gave birth to a child she gave away. The child, now grown, has come to the town and is asking questions. The banker must decide whether to help his wife or protect his name.

author: MS
premise: A woman who has written a novel that brought her fame is shunned by society when her authorship is revealed. Her husband, a man of science, is embarrassed by her success and forbids her to write again.

author: MS
premise: A small group of survivors in a future world decides to send a ship across the Atlantic to look for other people. The volunteers are a young couple, an old sailor, and a child who refuses to be left behind.
setting: A port in Cornwall, late in the twenty-first century

author: MS
premise: A young man who has always been told that his mother died at his birth learns that she is alive and has spent twenty years in an asylum. His father had her confined. The young man goes to see her.

author: MS
premise: In a future England slowly recovering from a pestilence, a woman who lost her children to the disease is asked to take in an orphan. She refuses. The orphan, a silent boy of six, keeps returning to her door.
setting: A village in Berkshire, late in the twenty-first century

author: OW
premise: A young baronet famous for never having done anything useful is informed by his solicitor that he must earn his own living for one year or forfeit his inheritance. His friends treat the condition as the most amusing scandal of the season. He accepts a post as private secretary to a cabinet minister's wife.

author: OW
premise: A respectable stockbroker receives an anonymous letter informing him that he is the rightful heir to a Portuguese marquisate. He dismisses it, then cannot stop thinking about it. His wife, who has always wished for a title, begins ordering new stationery before he has replied.
setting: A villa in Clapham and the City of London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A proud princess who has refused every suitor announces she will marry the man who can bring her something she has never seen. Kings bring jewels and wise men bring wonders. A poor shepherd boy brings her own reflection in a pool, and is thrown out of the palace.
setting: A kingdom of marble palaces beside a great forest

author: OW
premise: A celebrated hostess decides to give the most exclusive dinner of the season by inviting only people who have never met. The guests include a bishop, an actress, an explorer, and a young poet who has written a scandalous book. By the second course, everyone has discovered a secret about everyone else.
setting: A house in Grosvenor Square, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: An elderly duchess who has outlived three husbands decides to write her memoirs. Every family in society is terrified. Her nephew, who stands to inherit, is commissioned to edit the manuscript, and discovers that its most scandalous pages concern his own mother.
setting: A town house in Belgravia, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A little match-seller who has never owned anything beautiful finds a jewelled comb in the snow outside a palace. She keeps it, though she could sell it for bread. The princess who lost it searches the city, and the girl must decide whether to return it.
setting: A city of towers and snow in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A penniless young Irish poet arrives in London with one good coat and a letter of introduction to a duchess who has forgotten his family entirely. He talks his way into her drawing room, and within a month is invited everywhere except the one house he most wishes to enter.

author: OW
premise: An American heiress arrives in London determined to marry a duke. She discovers that the only unmarried duke is ninety and deaf. She resolves to marry him anyway, and his heir, a penniless nephew, sets out to prevent the match by courting her himself.

author: OW
premise: A king who has never laughed offers half his kingdom to anyone who can make him smile. Jesters, poets, and philosophers fail. A small kitchen maid who has never heard of the offer drops a tray of tarts in front of him.
setting: A kingdom of gardens and fountains

author: OW
premise: A celebrated composer of drawing-room ballads announces that he will write only serious music henceforth. His publisher despairs, his admirers desert him, and the one critic who has always despised his ballads is the first to call on him.

author: OW
premise: A young lord who has always been considered the dullest man in London is mistaken for a famous conversationalist by a visiting French journalist. He finds that people laugh at everything he says. He begins to believe himself brilliant, and his friends begin to worry.
setting: A club in St James's, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A clergyman of advanced views invites a celebrated aesthete to preach in his parish church. The aesthete accepts, and delivers a sermon on the beauty of sin. The congregation is scandalised, the bishop is outraged, and the church has never been so full.

author: OW
premise: A vain young peacock who lives in a royal garden believes himself the most beautiful creature in the world. When a plain grey bird begins to sing beneath the king's window, and the king prefers the song, the peacock must decide whether beauty is enough.
setting: A royal garden in an eastern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A young man who has always worshipped beauty falls in love with a woman of extraordinary plainness and extraordinary mind. His friends are horrified. He finds that his conversations with her are the only thing in his life that does not bore him.

author: OW
premise: An eccentric aunt who believes herself psychic holds a séance for her nephews. The spirit who appears claims to be their grandfather and demands that they each confess their sins. The nephews suspect a trick, but cannot discover who is playing it.

author: OW
premise: A young prince who has been raised in a tower and never seen the world is told on his eighteenth birthday that he may ask for one thing. He asks to see a poor man. The king, who has never seen one either, sends his ministers to search the city.
setting: A kingdom of towers and gardens

author: OW
premise: A young poet who has published a volume of decadent verse is invited to stay at a country house by a lady who admires his work. Her husband, a hunting squire, does not. Over a weekend the poet must survive the shooting, the dinners, and the husband.

author: OW
premise: A respectable family discovers that their butler is the author of a scandalous novel that has become the talk of London. They cannot dismiss him without admitting they have read it, and they cannot keep him without reading the sequel.

author: OW
premise: A golden fish in a palace fountain is granted the power of speech by a fairy. It uses its gift to tell the courtiers the truth about one another. The court is thrown into confusion, and the king must decide whether to silence the fish or to listen.
setting: A palace courtyard in a southern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A brilliant young barrister who has risen by charm and cleverness is offered a seat in Parliament by a great lady, on condition that he marry her niece. He does not love the niece. He loves the lady.

author: OW
premise: A beggar who sits every day at the gate of a cathedral is offered a crown by an angel, on condition that he give up his begging bowl. He refuses. The bishop, who has overheard, demands to know why.
setting: The gate of a cathedral in a medieval city

author: OW
premise: A young lady of fashion who has broken twelve engagements becomes engaged for the thirteenth time. Her fiancé is determined to be the first to reach the altar. Her mother is determined to prevent the thirteenth broken engagement for superstition's sake.

author: OW
premise: A dandy who is famous for never having been seen without a buttonhole loses his last flower on the morning of a great wedding. Every florist in London is closed. His pursuit of a single carnation leads him through the length and breadth of the city.

author: OW
premise: A poor woodcutter's daughter who weaves beautiful cloth is commanded by the queen to weave a robe that will make her the most beloved queen in the world. The girl weaves for a year, and the robe she delivers is plain grey.
setting: A cottage at the edge of a royal forest

author: OW
premise: A cynical old diplomat, retired to a house in Mayfair, entertains himself by giving his young great-nephew advice on how to succeed in society by saying the opposite of what he means. The nephew follows the advice literally, with results that astonish them both.

author: OW
premise: A young wife who discovers that her husband has paid the debts of a woman with a scandalous reputation believes him unfaithful. He refuses to explain. She resolves to attend the woman's ball, to confront her rival in her own house.

author: OW
premise: A committee of earnest ladies organising a lecture on the virtues of plain living invites a celebrated aesthete to speak against them, so that he may be refuted. His lecture converts the entire committee to the cult of beauty.
setting: A lecture hall in Kensington, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A water lily in a palace pool falls in love with the moon. The frogs mock her, and the goldfish tell her she is foolish. Every night she opens her petals to the moon, and every morning she closes them in sorrow.
setting: A palace pool in a moonlit garden

author: OW
premise: A young man who has always been told that he resembles his late father discovers that his father was not the man he believed. His mother, a great lady, refuses to say who was. His search for the truth leads him through the drawing rooms of London.

author: OW
premise: A shy young curate, mistaken for a famous explorer at a society reception, is asked to describe his adventures. He invents them on the spot. By the end of the evening, he has been invited to lead an expedition to Africa.

author: OW
premise: A clockmaker in a royal city builds a clock that can stop time. The king commands that it be used to make him live forever. The clockmaker warns him of the price. The king does not listen.
setting: A clockmaker's workshop in a royal city

author: OW
premise: A celebrated actress who has retired to marry a lord is invited to perform at a charity matinée. Her husband forbids it. She accepts anyway, and society must decide whether to applaud her or cut her.
setting: A theatre and a house in Mayfair, London, 1890s

author: OW
premise: A poor lace-maker who sells her lace at the palace gate is noticed by a vain duchess who orders a veil finer than any ever made. The lace-maker works for a year and goes blind in the making. The duchess wears the veil once and gives it away.
setting: A city of bridges in a southern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A brilliant and cynical young man who has never been in love bets his friends that he can make the coldest woman in London fall in love with him within a month. He wins the bet, and finds that he has lost something he cannot name.

author: OW
premise: A little lame boy who lives in a cottage at the edge of a great forest is visited each night by a white stag. He follows it into the forest, and finds a city where no one is lame, no one is old, and no one is happy.
setting: A great forest in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A wealthy philanthropist who has given away half his fortune is accused by a newspaper of buying his reputation. His wife, who has always found his charity tiresome, rushes to defend him, and discovers she believes in him after all.

author: OW
premise: A lady who has kept a diary of every compliment she has ever received loses it at a garden party. Every guest is terrified that their compliment will be read aloud. The young man who finds it is the only guest who never paid her one.

author: OW
premise: A young princess who has been told that she is the most beautiful girl in the world goes to the market in disguise to discover the truth. A blind woman who sells flowers tells her she sings beautifully, and the princess does not know whether to be pleased.
setting: A market in a royal city

author: OW
premise: A young man who has led a life of pleasure is told by his doctor that he has a year to live. He resolves to spend it doing good, and finds that good deeds are far more difficult than bad ones. The doctor's diagnosis proves to be mistaken.

author: OW
premise: An elderly baronet who has always claimed descent from a medieval king is presented with a genealogy showing that he is descended from the king's cook. His wife is devastated. He finds it the most interesting thing that has ever happened to him.

author: OW
premise: A shepherd finds a silver bell in a field after a storm. When he rings it, every animal on the hillside kneels. The lord of the valley demands the bell. The shepherd must decide whether to give it up, or to ring it in the lord's hall.
setting: A valley at the edge of a great plain

author: OW
premise: A married woman of fashion receives a letter from a young admirer threatening to kill himself if she does not see him. She does not take it seriously. Her husband, who opens her letters, does.

author: OW
premise: A young man who has failed at every profession decides to become a critic, on the principle that criticism requires no talent. His first review is so cruel and so brilliant that he becomes famous overnight, and every artist in London wants to be insulted by him.

author: OW
premise: A miser who lives in a tower above a town counts his gold every night by the light of a single candle. One winter evening a child knocks on his door to ask for a light for her mother's lamp. He gives it grudgingly, and finds he cannot stop thinking about the child.
setting: A tower above a town in a northern kingdom

author: OW
premise: A young heiress who has been brought up to believe that wealth is vulgar falls in love with a penniless artist, and is disappointed to learn that he wishes to be rich. She resolves to teach him the beauty of poverty. He resolves to teach her the poverty of beauty.

author: OW
premise: A dinner party is thrown into chaos when the guest of honour, a celebrated talker, arrives with nothing to say. The hostess, desperate, begins to entertain the table herself, and discovers that she is far more amusing than her guest.

author: OW
premise: A rich man's son and a poor man's son are born on the same night in the same city. A fairy grants each a gift. The rich man's son is given beauty, the poor man's son a kind heart. Twenty years later, they meet at the palace gate.

author: OW
premise: An old organ in a cathedral that has not been played for a hundred years begins to play by itself on Christmas Eve. The bishop forbids anyone to listen. A little choirboy who cannot sleep creeps into the cathedral to hear it.
setting: A cathedral in an old city

author: OW
premise: A young man returns from three years in Australia to find that his fiancée has married his best friend. She explains that she believed him dead. He suspects that she simply grew bored. Both explanations, he decides, are equally flattering.

author: OW
premise: A proud young swan who believes herself above the other birds on the royal lake refuses to share her bread with the ducks. When winter comes and the lake freezes, the ducks are the only ones who know where the open water lies.

author: VW
premise: The daughter of a bishop, twenty-six and unmarried, keeps her father's household and answers his correspondence. A young curate who comes to read to the bishop treats her opinions as worth contradicting, and she finds herself, for the first time, arguing about something she cares for.
setting: A cathedral close in the west of England, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has kept house for her brother, a country doctor, since their parents died goes with him to a medical congress in Paris. At the dinners and lectures she is taken for his wife, and finds that strangers listen to her more readily than anyone at home ever has.

author: VW
premise: A young woman's first year in London, working as a typist and living in a hostel, is seen through the people who notice her in passing: a bus conductor, a clergyman's wife who runs the hostel, a young man in the office, her mother reading her letters in Yorkshire.

author: VW
premise: A woman who teaches evening classes for working men falls in love with one of her students, a printer with a wife and children. She tells no one and continues to teach him. He brings her a book he has printed himself, and she does not know what he means by it.
setting: A working men's college in Camden, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A widow who lost her only son at the Somme goes each morning to feed the ducks in a London park, at the hour he used to walk there before the war. A boy of about the same age begins to sit on the next bench, and she cannot decide whether she wants him to speak.

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged Englishwoman wintering in Madeira with her invalid husband befriends a young Portuguese woman who sells lace in the hotel courtyard. Through the girl's talk of her family and her hopes, the Englishwoman sees how small and comfortable her own life has been.

author: VW
premise: A young schoolmaster from a northern industrial town spends a weekend at the country house of a pupil's family. The beauty of the house and the ease of the people enchant him, and he discovers on Sunday evening that he has been invited chiefly to make up numbers.

author: VW
premise: A woman's life from childhood to old age is glimpsed in a series of moments: a summer at the seaside, a proposal in a garden, a death in a nursing home, a walk in the park with a grandchild. The moments do not quite make a story, and she wonders whether they make a life.

author: VW
premise: A woman who has organised a charity concert spends the day of the performance soothing musicians, arranging chairs, and worrying about her husband, who has lost money and not told her. In the evening the hall fills, and she watches the faces of people she has known for twenty years.
setting: A concert hall and a house in Kensington, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A party of English visitors in Norway takes a steamer up a fjord to see a glacier. On board, a widower and a woman who has never married fall into a conversation that neither of them expected, while the younger members of the party quarrel about poetry.

author: VW
premise: Two sisters, one married and one not, spend a week together at the seaside with the married sister's children. The unmarried sister realises that she envies her sister nothing. The married sister realises that she envies her sister everything.

author: VW
premise: A woman travelling by train to her sister's funeral finds herself sharing a compartment with a young soldier going home on leave. They speak only of the weather and the countryside, and by the end of the journey each knows something about the other that neither has told anyone.
setting: A railway carriage between London and the north, 1916

author: VW
premise: A schoolmistress on her day off walks from her lodgings to the National Gallery, where she stands for a long time before one painting. Her thoughts move between the painting, the girls she teaches, and a letter in her bag that she has not yet opened.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has nursed her grandmother through her last illness inherits a small legacy and spends it on a journey to Sicily alone. Her relations disapprove. In Palermo she meets no one and talks to no one, and is happier than she has ever been.

author: VW
premise: A young woman from a family of lawyers is expected to marry her father's most promising pupil. He is earnest, admiring, and rather dull. She accepts him because there is no reason not to, and spends the engagement looking for a reason.
setting: Lincoln's Inn and a house in Kensington, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: An old schoolmaster who taught a generation of boys who went to the war sits in his empty classroom at the end of the last term before his retirement. He reads the names carved into the desks, and remembers the boys, and the boys he has forgotten.

author: VW
premise: A charwoman who cleans the offices of a firm of solicitors moves through the empty rooms early on a winter morning. She reads the letters on the desks, looks out at the river, and thinks about her son in Canada and her husband in the churchyard.
setting: An office near the Thames, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A pension in the south of France is full of English guests waiting out the winter: a retired governess, a young man recovering from an illness, a widow and her spinster daughter, a painter who is failing. Over a month of meals and walks, the guests settle into one another's lives.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has spent her life looking after her widowed father announces that she intends to take rooms of her own and work for a living. Her father, a distinguished historian, is wounded and bewildered. Her aunts consider the matter a family crisis.

author: VW
premise: A crowded omnibus crosses London on a wet afternoon, and the city is glimpsed through the passengers: a typist thinking of her lover, an old man counting his change, a mother with a sick child, a clergyman composing a sermon. The bus reaches its terminus, and they scatter.
setting: An omnibus route from Hammersmith to the City, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged politician walks from his club to the House of Commons on the morning of an important debate. He thinks of his speech, of his wife, of a woman he loved in his youth, and of whether any of it matters.

author: VW
premise: A young Englishwoman visiting her married sister in Italy is introduced to the circle of English artists and writers who live there. She finds them brilliant and cruel, and is drawn to the one among them who is neither.

author: VW
premise: A young man who works in a government office and writes poetry in the evenings meets, at a lecture, a young woman who works for a charity. They argue about everything. They begin to meet every week to continue the argument.

author: VW
premise: A young typist on her lunch hour sits in a city churchyard eating sandwiches. She watches the pigeons and the clerks and the old men on the benches, and thinks about the young man who has asked her to the theatre, and whether she will go.
setting: A churchyard in the City of London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A middle-aged woman who has never left England travels to Greece with her brother, a classical scholar. Among the ruins she discovers that she has a feeling for beauty her brother lacks, and that she has been living his life instead of her own.

author: VW
premise: An old lady who has been the centre of a famous literary circle is visited by a young journalist who wishes to write about her. She tells him stories that are not quite true, and watches him believe them.

author: VW
premise: A woman sorting her late mother's clothes on a winter evening finds in a coat pocket a theatre ticket from a year she cannot place. She sits on the floor among the clothes and tries to imagine the evening, and the woman her mother was before she was born.

author: VW
premise: A young English governess travelling with her employer's family to a villa in Spain finds herself the only person in the household who speaks the language. The family depend on her, and the villagers trust her, and she begins to feel for the first time that she belongs somewhere.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has been engaged for a year to a dull and kind man breaks the engagement on the evening before a family dinner. She must sit through the dinner with her parents, her aunts, and her former fiancé, who has not been told.

author: VW
premise: A woman who has worked for thirty years as a housekeeper in a great house is remembered, after her death, by the family she served, the servants she ruled, and the village where she was born. Each remembers a different woman.
setting: A great house in Sussex, 1890s to 1920s

author: VW
premise: A retired colonel spends a day in his London club, reading the newspapers, eating his lunch, and talking to no one. In the afternoon he receives a telegram announcing that his son is getting married. He does not know the bride.
setting: A club in St James's, London, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A young man recovering from an illness is sent by his doctors to a hotel in the mountains of Switzerland. Among the invalids and their families he meets a young woman who is not ill at all, but who has come to escape her family.
setting: A hotel in the Swiss Alps, 1900s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has always wanted to be a painter is told by her family that she must marry, and by her teacher that she has no talent. She paints anyway, in an attic studio she has cleared herself, and the paintings are seen by no one.

author: VW
premise: A party of English visitors to a Mediterranean island climbs a mountain on a hot afternoon. On the way, they quarrel, flirt, confide in one another, and fall silent before the view. On the way down, nothing is quite the same between them.

author: VW
premise: A young man who has been engaged to a beautiful and conventional girl finds himself drawn to her plain and unconventional friend, who works for a living and laughs at him. He does not know how to stop.
setting: London and a house in the country, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A woman's friendships with three other women, from school to old age, are seen in a series of meetings: a tea party, a wedding, a funeral, a chance encounter in a railway station. Each meeting changes what the others mean.

author: VW
premise: A young man who has come to London from the provinces to make his name as a writer spends a day walking the city, looking for a room, a job, and something to write about. By evening he has found none of them, and has seen everything.

author: VW
premise: An Englishwoman who married a Frenchman and has lived in France for twenty years returns to London for her mother's funeral. She finds that she is a stranger in her own country, and that her sisters regard her as a foreigner.
setting: London, with a life in France, 1920s

author: VW
premise: A young woman who works in a bookshop is courted by a wealthy customer who knows nothing about books. She is tempted by his kindness and his money. Her friend, a struggling poet, tells her she would be selling herself.
setting: A bookshop in Charing Cross Road, London, 1910s

author: VW
premise: A woman who has lived in the same London street for forty years walks its length on the day before the house is to be sold. She remembers the people who lived in each house, and the people she was when she knew them.

author: VW
premise: A young woman travelling with her father in Egypt meets a young archaeologist who is excavating a tomb. She is fascinated by his work, and by him. Her father, who wishes her to marry a cousin at home, decides to cut the journey short.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who has just come down from university returns to her parents' house and finds that nothing has changed and that she has changed completely. She must decide whether to stay and be a dutiful daughter or leave and find work.

author: VW
premise: A family is seen through the years of the war: a son at the front, a daughter in a hospital, a mother at home, a father in his office. Their letters cross, their visits fail, and at the end of the war they find they have become strangers to one another.

author: VW
premise: A young mother takes her small son to the park on a spring morning. As he plays, she thinks of her own mother, her husband, her friends, the book she meant to write, and the person she thought she would become.

author: VW
premise: A young man on a walking tour of the Alps with a friend falls in love with a young woman at an inn. His friend, who is in love with him, watches. The young woman does not notice either of them.

author: VW
premise: An old couple who have been married for fifty years give a party to celebrate. Their children and grandchildren gather. During the party, the wife slips away to the garden and thinks about the man she might have married instead.

author: VW
premise: A young woman who works in a department store spends her day serving customers, eating her lunch in the staff room, and thinking about the young man she met at a dance. On her way home, she sees him with another girl.

author: VW
premise: An English family takes a villa on the Italian lakes for the summer. The eldest daughter falls in love with an Italian count, the youngest son runs wild in the hills, and the mother writes letters home that say nothing of what is happening.

author: VW
premise: A young woman cataloguing the library of a great house for its new owner finds the house's history written in the margins of its books: a girl's pencilled verses, a soldier's notes, a mother's list of children's illnesses. She begins to feel she knows the family better than its heir does.

author: VW
premise: A young woman returning to England after a year in India with her family sits on the deck of the ship as it approaches the coast. She thinks of what she has seen and what she will tell her friends, and realises that she will tell them nothing.
setting: A ship in the English Channel, 1900s
